#6747. All About Lana Del Rey’s Husband, Jeremy Dufrene

On Saturday, Sept. 7, 2024, Lana Del Rey officially debuted her relationship with Jeremy Dufrene, bringing him as her plus one to the wedding of model Karen Elson and Lee Foster in New York City. The couple walked out of Electric Lady Studios hand-in-hand wearing big smiles.

Del Rey was also wearing a satin blue halter dress with white ballet flats while Dufrene wore a blue suit with a white button-up shirt and brown shoes.

Weeks later, they got married. On Sept. 26, 2024, People reported that the couple obtained a marriage certificate. They had their ceremony that same day. Here’s everything to know about Jeremy Dufrene, Del Rey’s husband.

Dufrene operates as a captain for a tour boat company in Des Allemands, Louisiana, close to New Orleans, called Airboat Tours by Arthur. The tours focus on local wildlife and apparently the company has a good reputation. In his bio, Dufrene says he once worked at a chemical plant and enjoys shrimping.

“After a little convincing by his family, he got his captain’s license and started running tours,” it continues.

According to People, Dufrene has three children, a son and two daughters.

Del Rey made an appearance in one of Dufrene’s social media posts in 2019 after taking a tour of his while visiting for the BUKU Music + Art Project festival. In a now private post on Instagram, Dufrene wrote, “I never know who I can run across on my tours but always a pleasure @lanadelrey.”

She also shared shots of him in Facebook posts, captioning them, “Jeremy lemme be captain at Arthur’s Air Boat Tours.”

In May 2024, Del Rey reportedly took another tour. She tagged him in the caption of a photo with friends.

In August 2024, they were spotted at Reading & Leeds Festival and were seen in a video on TikTok holding hands. They then headed to London for a visit to Harrod’s and a local pub. After the images circulated, Del Rey denied she and Dufrene were dating in a comment on TikTok, simply writing “No,” on a video about their alleged relationship. It ended up later being a yes.

People reported on Sept. 26, 2024, that the couple obtained a marriage license from the Lafourche Parish Clerk of Court on September 23. They had 30 days from that date to tie the knot.

The same day as People broke the news, Del Rey and Dufrene got married in Des Allemandes, Louisiana. They had their ceremony at the bayou where Dufrene works. Photos surfaced of Del Rey walking with her father there, wearing a ruffle neckline gown with a full skirt. She had a blue ribbon tied in her hair, which was styled in a side ponytail.

Another source told People that the couple chose a place close to their hearts for the ceremony.

“The wedding ceremony and reception were both held in the same bayou where Jeremy operates his swamp boats tours,” said the insider. “This is where they first met. It’s a special place for them. It was a beautiful, relaxed and family-focused wedding. The focus was just on their love story.”

The source shared more about their love story, saying that Del Rey and Dufrene “initially met a few years ago the first time and then reconnected earlier this year.”

They added, “It’s been kind of a whirlwind romance, but Lana’s close friends hoped she would get married. Jeremy is different from the men that Lana meets in the entertainment world. He’s a great guy. He’s charming and charismatic in a Southern way, very much a gentleman and he treats Lana really well. She’s an old soul.”

Del Rey reportedly found her dress for the ceremony at a local boutique, Vintage Market by Trashy Diva, in New Orleans, and purchased it that May—months before she went public with her and Dufrene’s relationship.

A source told TMZ that it’s “unclear whether Lana strolled into the store specifically hunting for a wedding dress, but after trying on a bunch of other stuff, she ended up falling for the dress she spotted in the window.”

The insider didn’t know the price, but they estimated that $400 is the “typical price range for wedding dresses at the store, which features curated styles from the 1920s to Y2K.”

On October 25, Del Rey attended the InStyle Imagemaker Awards and was asked about her marriage for the first time publicly.

She simply replied, “It’s good. We’re happy.”

On Saturday, December 7, Del Rey attended Variety’s Hitmakers Brunch and spoke in honor of producer Jack Antonoff as he was named Producer of the Decade. During her speech, Del Rey opened up about her husband and how Antonoff’s relationship with his then-wife, Margaret Qualley, inspired her to connect with Dufrene.

“Most of all, I’m grateful for him for his example that he gave me in his marriage to Margaret,” the singer said, after thanking him for his work on her music. “I saw the way he looked at her when he met her, and he’s a big reason why I waited so long to get married and why I met my amazing husband.”

She also admitted that having a high-profile career can make finding an authentic partner difficult.

“I really feel like there’s kind of a singer’s curse around meeting an honest partner who has no skin in the game, no dog in the race,” she said. “And it’s super nerve-racking to have to hold onto an innocent perception of how things could go when you’re in an industry where maybe your values or your morals don’t quite match up with what’s going on.”

Del Rey added, “Especially when people think that you probably don’t have any morals or values.”

She then thanked Antonoff for “maybe helping other people look at me in a way that is a little bit closer to how I perceive myself.”

In a carousel of pictures posted on April 4, the singer revealed some intimate moments with Dufrene. She was also celebrating upcoming shows at Stagecoach music festival. In the caption, she wrote, “This has been such a crazy nine months and I’m so blessed that come the 25th, It will have been a year since I got to headline Coachella. Thank you to my buddies over there at the festival for letting me play my new songs this year for you—and to my amazing band helping me kick things off with rehearsals this week.”

The carousel included a picture from a birthday party where she and Dufrene are wearing matching tiaras, as well as the crocodile-themed birthday cake referencing Dufrene’s business. There was also a sweet photo of Dufrene embracing Del Rey from behind.

The couple seemed to be enjoying New York City in early spring and summer, based on a few posts from Del Rey. On May 7, she tagged Dufrene in a few clips and photos from a jazz club, writing they brought “a little taste of New Orleans” to the city.

On June 8, she shared a carousel of photos, many taken in New York City, including a mirror selfie with a bunch of friends where it looks like Dufrene is standing behind her.

During her tour stop in Cardiff, Wales, on June 23, Del Rey made her affection for Dufrene very public. While performing “Stars Fell on Alabama,” she briefly stepped to the side of the stage to kiss her husband. After the moment of PDA, she returned to the mic and resumed singing.

On July 31, 2025, Del Rey offered a rare glimpse of her and Dufrene’s private September 2024 wedding. She posted a photo from the ceremony on Instagram, featuring herself in a flowy white gown with a bow in her hair as she held hands with Dufrene, who wore a black suit.

On September 26, Del Rey posted a carousel of images from her wedding to celebrate their anniversary. She included shots with Dufrene posing on an airboat and with friends and family, including Jack Antonoff and Margaret Qualley.

On October 5, Del Rey and Dufrene stepped out together for Valentino’s Paris Fashion Week runway show, marking one of their few public appearances since getting married. The couple arrived holding hands, with Del Rey wearing a lilac floor-length gown accented with a bow at the waist, while Dufrene opted for a navy jacket and matching trousers with tan boots.

Inside the event, the pair shared a kiss from their front-row seats.

Del Rey brought Dufrene as her date to the Ralph Lauren fashion show on Feb. 10, 2026. In a sweet photo from the event, she smiled happily while hanging onto her husband’s arm.

On February 17, Del Rey posted a series of Instagram Stories tied to the release of her new single, “White Feather Hawk Tail Deer Hunter.” One clip opened with footage from a cartoon, before cutting to a video of Del Rey and Dufrene dancing as the song played.

In the clip, she wore a brown sweater and an ivory skirt while Dufrene stood behind her in a khaki jacket. Del Rey released “White Feather Hawk Tail Deer Hunter” in full that day, tagging Dufrene in the announcement post as a co-writer on the track.

On March 27, Del Rey posted new pictures with Dufrene from their life together, including a trip to Home Depot, time on his boat, and flipping through wedding book memories. In the caption, she wrote, “Happy birthday week to the sweetest guy I know ❤️🦆”

The couple was spotted in Los Angeles on April 17, enjoying a lunch date at The Ivy restaurant. Del Rey was wearing a striped shirt under an off-the-shoulder sweatshirt with denim shorts and ballet shoes. Dufrene was in a white T-shirt, khakis, and a black baseball hat. They appeared to have been out shopping. Del Rey carried her leather purse, and Dufrene had a shopping bag.

On August 27, Del Rey and Dufrene were photographed on a shopping trip in Los Angeles, where they stopped by a Ralph Lauren store.

Del Rey wore a white tank top with straight-leg jeans and an open light-wash denim shirt, finishing her look with white sneakers. Dufrene kept things casual in a gray T-shirt, black shorts, sneakers, a camouflage baseball cap, and sunglasses.

On September 27, Del Rey celebrated two years of marriage to Dufrene with an Instagram carousel featuring memories from their relationship, including footage of the couple kissing during their wedding ceremony.

“Hi husband, happy second anniversary... Thank you for making everywhere I’ve ever lived feel like home again. And also to our lil fam...literally everything we do is the best. Xo,” she wrote.

Dufrene shared his own anniversary tribute, writing, “Happy Anniversary to the most Beautiful and Precious lil wife. I love you so much.”

On November 20, Del Rey shared a series of photos from a Grand Theft Auto VI launch party in Miami, where she was joined by her husband. “Cruisin,” she captioned the Instagram carousel, which included photos of the couple posing together at the event.

For the occasion, Del Rey carried a custom pink Hermès Birkin inspired by the video game and created by Privé Porter. The bag featured Swarovski-crystal designs referencing Vice City, the fictional Miami-inspired setting of the game. Del Rey also has a song, “Crazy for You,” on the Grand Theft Auto VI soundtrack, and she and Dufrene reportedly voice fictional radio hosts in the game.

#6746. Enterprise AI Spending Outpaces Adoption Growth, Report Finds

Enterprise AI spending is growing faster than the number of organizations paying for it, according to a new Menlo Ventures report that points to a shift from buying access for employees to financing work performed by agents.

The venture capital firm's 2026 State of Enterprise AI report estimates deployment spending reached a $176.8 billion annualized run rate by September, up from $33 billion in 2025. The share of enterprises paying for AI rose from 55% to 65%.

A larger bill can reflect broader use inside an organization, but it does not independently establish that the additional work is useful or profitable.

Menlo's methodology describes revenue figures as annualized run rates. The $176.8 billion estimate therefore should not be read as $176.8 billion already spent during the first nine months of 2026.

The report also distinguishes unusually heavy spenders from the typical respondent. Average reported spending reached 4.7 times the prior year's level, while the median reached 2.2 times. That gap suggests a smaller group of large spenders drove the average substantially.

The practical implication is that an industry growth figure may be a poor benchmark for an individual organization's budget. Buyers need to understand their own workload growth and the results it produces.

"Agents are changing the economics of software," Menlo principal Derek Xiao said in the firm's announcement.

Menlo reports that agents account for 80% of tokens on OpenRouter, a service providing access to multiple models. That measures activity on one platform, rather than all enterprise AI use. Token consumption also measures processing volume, rather than completed business outcomes.

An agent that makes repeated attempts can consume more resources without delivering proportionately more value. For procurement teams, the relevant comparison is consequently the cost of completing acceptable work, including the review it requires.

Menlo estimates that Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google capture 69% of enterprise AI deployment spending. That measure is distinct from their shares of enterprise language-model API spending, a narrower category. The figures should not be used interchangeably.

The report draws on a Morning Consult survey of nearly 400 U.S. enterprise decision-makers responsible for more than $4 billion in AI spending. Market totals are modeled estimates informed by surveys, public filings, and third-party reports. Menlo discloses investments in Anthropic and OpenRouter.

A separate announcement from Information Services Group describes buyers putting more emphasis on the economics and reliability of production deployments. ISG says ongoing security and observability work remains necessary as organizations scale.

That provides a useful distinction between market demand and business value. Suppliers can generate growing revenue while customers still determine which deployments justify the cost.

For enterprise leaders, the new spending estimate strengthens the case for examining usage beyond license counts. It leaves the harder purchasing question with the customer: How much worthwhile work did the increased spending actually buy?

Menlo's State of Enterprise AI report is available here.

John K. Waters is the editor in chief of a number of Converge360.com sites, with a focus on high-end development, AI and future tech. He's been writing about cutting-edge technologies and culture of Silicon Valley for more than two decades, and he's written more than a dozen books. He also co-scripted the documentary film Silicon Valley: A 100 Year Renaissance, which aired on PBS.  He can be reached at [email protected].

New research suggests that the value of AI should be measured not only by the work it eliminates, but also by the instructional insight and human connection it preserves.

AI-powered vulnerability research is contributing to a major increase in security updates, raising concerns that IT teams could fall behind as patching demands grow, according to cybersecurity company ThreatDown.

Sign-in problems account for up to 53% of help desk tickets at individual enterprises, but network issues can take significantly longer to resolve, according to a recent study from ControlUp.

A vendor coalition built on an Okta-developed blueprint is proposing a shared architecture for discovering, governing, monitoring, and containing enterprise AI agents.

#6745. Hunter Schafer Masterfully Combines Decades of Prada Fashion

Something old, something new, lots of Prada, and something blue

The Blade Runner franchise imagines a bleak dystopian future, one where the world has been ravaged by nuclear war and humans are burdened with inequality and threatened by rogue robots. But if everyone dressed like Hunter Schafer, how bad could it really be?

While promoting her new miniseries, Blade Runner 2099—which serves as a sequel to the Blade Runner (1982) and Blade Runner 2049 (2017) movies—Schafer has been on a hot streak of futuristic, otherworldly looks.

So far, she’s worn everything from a neon-green Nihl hoodie covered in beaded florals to a double-layer Lii minidress that appeared to peel open from the back. Now, her latest ensemble plays with time in a different way—by looking space-age, sure, but also by uniting decades of fashion history.

At the Blade Runner 2099 photocall in London earlier today, Schafer stepped out in a pop-art inspired look that combined periods of Prada fashion.

Styled by Dara, Schafer embraced the exposed-underwear trend with a satin, cerulean bra, which was paired with a white wrap-around midi skirt with a patch of neon-green color. Both were pulled directly from the Prada Spring/Summer 2027 ready-to-wear collection by Miuccia Prada and Raf Simons.

While Schafer has long been a supporter of the storied Italian brand, here, she and Dara pulled out a reference for the true fans, layering on a transparent, PVC raincoat pulled from Prada’s Fall 2002 collection.

With its thick black trim, the vinyl outerwear could have been plucked straight from the pages of a comic book. And to match the edges, the coat was cinched with an inky leather belt, while Schafer wore a pair of pointy black heels down low. For a finishing touch, she rocked electric-blue eyeshadow that winked to the color of her bra.

Sometimes, it can be hard to feel optimistic about the future. But at least Schafer is here to imagine one that’s wonderfully colorful, fun, and stylish.

#6742. The Launch: November’s Must-Know Fashion News

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Fall is in full swing, and with it, so is the fashion industry. As the leaves continue to turn and preparations for the holiday season get serious, brands are finding new ways to celebrate with exciting new capsules, collaborations, and stocking-worthy releases. Look no further than J.J. Martin, whose new book, Table Energy, explores the art of Italian entertaining, and Rimowa x Maison Margiela, which turns travel into something even more desirable. Plus, there’s plenty of reason to get out and shop, with the likes of L/Uniform, Danielle Frankel, and Bulgari all opening new storefronts. Below, all the fashion news to know this month.

Where: Online at gap.com and in select Gap stores

Why: Zac Posen is keeping things simple this winter season—and the latest GapStudio wardrobe is edited to just 12 pieces. The designer’s capsule gives familiar staples a sharper feel through sleek silhouettes, precise tailoring, and touches of unexpected texture like a playful teddy bear coat rendered in a cozy caramel fabric. Other highlights include elevated essentials that Posen has prioritized at the brand: a turtleneck maxi dress, a sleek poplin shirt, and high-rise seamed stirrup jeans. “For winter 2026, we wanted to move beyond traditional occasion wear with versatile pieces designed to be worn from day to night,” Posen said of the collection, which came to life on singer EJAE in the accompanying campaign, in a statement. “There’s still that level of drama with thoughtful tailoring and exaggerated lines, but it’s balanced by a focused palette that feels elegant and wearable.”

Why: Parisian leather goods label L/Uniform is making its New York debut with a flagship on the Upper East Side. Following boutiques in Paris and Tokyo, the store marks the brand’s first American address with founder Jeanne Signoles working with architect Jakob Sprenger to create a space that balances the polish of a boutique with the practical spirit at the heart of the label. “Opening a store in New York was a priority for me from the very beginning,” Signoles says. “I always felt that L/Uniform naturally belonged here, with the city’s energy, its independence, and its very strong connection to everyday life. Our bags are made to be used—to work, to travel, to accompany daily life.”

Why: A historic Tribeca landmark is the setting for Danielle Frankel’s new flagship. At 6 Harrison Street, the bridal house has created a 12,000-square-foot space where original architectural character meets a considered, contemporary interior by Augusta Hoffman Studio. #6741. Which Christmas Tree Is Right for Your Home? Experts Break It Down

Consider this your shortcut to finding the perfect holiday centerpiece.

Holiday decorating is supposed to be a joyous event, but picking the right tree can be surprisingly complicated. There’s a lot of height, circumference, and branch density variation—some people like a full, fluffy look, while others opt for a more minimal tree—and don’t even entice us with the real versus faux debate.

The truth is, any tree can be beautiful in the right setting, so if you’re feeling unsure about which one fits your home, we’ve created the ultimate guide on which tree is right for your holiday centerpiece. Ahead, we're sharing the most popular types of Christmas trees for every household.

The Fraser fir is one of the most popular types of Christmas tree, especially for households east of the Rocky Mountains. Firs, in general, are some of the most common trees grown for the holiday season, says Ward Dilmore, founder of Petrus Landscaping in California. There's a good reason for this: They have a perfect balance of deep green color and even, stiff branching, he says, which makes them a breeze to decorate.

Canaan fir trees often get compared to Fraser and balsam firs, thanks to their similar growing patterns and branch density, but this variety has a major benefit above the rest: needle retention. It sheds less than other firs, which means less cleanup for you.

Often a home for many birds, including woodpeckers, the eastern white pine is fluffy and fast-growing. With foliage that's thin, delicate, and silvery-green, this tree is best paired with lightweight ornaments and minimal decorations.

A classic type of Christmas tree, the noble fir is native to the Cascade and Pacific Coast mountain ranges of the Northwestern United States. With strong branches, this tree ensures your precious family heirlooms won't be at risk of falling, and the long peak is ideal for an oversized tree topper.

The Arizona cypress is the most drought-tolerant evergreen out there—with the right care, this type of Christmas tree can last longer than other evergreens. With its thick, layered branches and lacy silver-blue foliage, this tree is a beautiful alternative to the silver fir.

You’ll find this bushy type of Christmas tree primarily in Southern states, according to the Real Christmas Tree Board. Thanks to its stout branches, it should have no problem holding up your heaviest ceramic ornaments. It also has a piney fragrance and keeps its needles well throughout the season, as long as you give it plenty of water to drink.

Also known as a red fir, these striking trees are one of the rarest types of Christmas trees, says horticulturist and botanical designer Nathan Heinrich. They're slow-growing, and only a few farmers and harvesters have permits in California and Oregon to harvest them in the wild each year, he explains. "The reason these trees make such perfect Christmas trees is because they have such perfectly spaced, open, elegant branches that make hanging ornaments and lights easy," Heinrich says.

Like Miracle on 34th Street and peppermint hot chocolate, the balsam fir is a holiday classic. It's also the most fragrant of all types of Christmas trees, according to the Real Christmas Tree Board. You can find these at Christmas tree farms in Canada, New England, the upper Great Lakes, and Pennsylvania, along with lots of retail locations east of the Rocky Mountains.

The Scotch pine often flies under the radar, but it's a designer-favorite Christmas tree choice, and it has great needle retention. "With vibrant green and durable needles that resist shedding, it's low maintenance," says New York designer Artem Kropovinsky of interior design studio Arsight. "Its robust branches accommodate even the heaviest ornaments, and its dense appearance gives rooms a fuller, festive look."

The trees you see in lots often have been pruned and sheared into the quintessential Christmas tree shape, explains Lisa Tadewaldt, an ISA-certified arborist and owner of Portland, Oregon–based Urban Forest Professionals. She recommends getting a permit and cutting a tree that's native to your area down in the forest. In the Pacific Northwest, her favorite tree in its natural form is a grand fir. "It is going to give more Charlie Brown vibes than Hallmark Christmas vibes, but it has a flat needle pattern that gives it an air of elegance that balances out the thinner, more homespun branching pattern," she says.

With its signature bluish needles, the robust blue spruce has a full, triangular shape, says Kropovinsky. "Apart from its signature color, this tree releases a fresh scent similar to frosty woodlands," he says. Bonus for pet owners: "Given the tree's pointed foliage, pets often steer clear of it."

With its flexible needles and twigs, the Eastern red cedar doesn't hold ornaments all that well. But don’t let that deter you! If your heart is set on this hardy juniper, it looks great draped with lights, says ISA-certified master arborist Blake Watkins, operations partner at Monster Tree Service.

The Douglas fir is a type of Christmas tree that is synonymous with the Pacific Northwest, but is available at holiday tree markets nationwide. It's also one of the more affordable types of Christmas trees you can find. "Dark green foliage and hanging needles make this tree gorgeous even without ornaments," Watkins says.

The concolor fir (also called the white fir) is the type of tree you'd like to sidle up next to with a mug of mulled wine. While many trees have pine scents, this one actually gives off a citrus aroma that has garnered it some devoted fans, according to the Michigan State University Extension. Looks-wise, its branches have long, silvery, bluish-green needles.

#6740. Phishing Threats Totaled 7.3 Billion in Q3 2026

E-mail phishing threats reached 7.3 billion in Q3 2026, with September activity increasing 41% from August, according to Microsoft Threat Intelligence.

According to a report from Microsoft Threat Intelligence and the Microsoft Defender Security Research Team, phishing detections reached nearly 3 billion in September alone.

The findings also highlighted changes in attacker techniques, including business-service impersonation, credential theft, and social engineering through Microsoft Teams.

The Redmond-based firm recognized approximately 129 million malicious messages spoofing the sender domains of tracked business services during Q3.

DocuSign was the most frequently spoofed brand in September, accounting for 29% of the month's tracked spoofing activity. Adobe, SurveyMonkey, and Barracuda also experienced increases toward the end of the quarter.

The research found that some malicious messages were delivered despite failing e-mail authentication checks and being identified as threats.

In September, tenant- or user-level security overrides applied to 63% of these messages with a recorded security outcome — most involved tenant-level exceptions.

Microsoft warned that overly broad exceptions intended to support legitimate business communications can weaken protection against impersonation attacks.

The company emphasized that these findings do not establish whether recipients opened the messages or whether accounts were compromised.

Microsoft also recorded approximately 141,000 malicious Teams call attempts during Q3.

Attackers increasingly used ordinary personal names instead of explicitly impersonating IT support personnel. Such display names accounted for 46% of an observed sample in July, rising to 88% in September.

Meanwhile, QR code phishing declined 67% compared to Q2, totaling roughly 12.1 million attacks.

CAPTCHA-gated phishing activity increased toward the end of the quarter, reaching 3.1 million detected attacks in September. SVG attachments played a significant role in the increase.

Credential theft remained the primary objective of malicious attachment campaigns, with approximately 94% to 96% of payload-based attacks directing users to phishing sites or fraudulent sign-in pages.

Microsoft recommended reviewing Exchange Online Protection and Defender for Office 365 configurations, enabling Safe Links and Safe Attachments, and strengthening authentication protections.

The company also advised organizations to review security exceptions and verify the identities of external Teams contacts before responding to suspicious requests.

For more information, go to the Microsoft blog post.

New research suggests that the value of AI should be measured not only by the work it eliminates, but also by the instructional insight and human connection it preserves.

AI-powered vulnerability research is contributing to a major increase in security updates, raising concerns that IT teams could fall behind as patching demands grow, according to cybersecurity company ThreatDown.

Sign-in problems account for up to 53% of help desk tickets at individual enterprises, but network issues can take significantly longer to resolve, according to a recent study from ControlUp.

A vendor coalition built on an Okta-developed blueprint is proposing a shared architecture for discovering, governing, monitoring, and containing enterprise AI agents.

#6738. “It Was Never About Fashion”: Emily in Paris’s Costume Designer Reveals the Method to Her Madness

“Emily in Paris: Fashion Without Rules,” a new show at SCAD Fashion in Atlanta, is devoted to the series’s unique style

Emily in Paris premiered when audiences needed it most. The Netflix original, created by Sex and the City producer Darren Star, offered an escapist fantasy: a young girl trying to find love and success in Paris in October 2020. The show functioned as a reprieve from the pandemic, a dreamy alternative in which we could vicariously live through Emily (Lily Collins) as she gallivanted around the City of Light. It was and still is delectably digestible television.

The love for Emily in Paris was anything but unanimous. Critics wasted no time tearing the show apart, with some targeting its depictions of French culture or claiming the script lacked the bite of Star’s previous television shows. The criticism extended to Emily’s idiosyncratic wardrobe, with some writing that the clothing leaned hard on American stereotypes of French fashion or looked cartoonish, with clashing patterns and bright colors. Costume designer Marylin Fitoussi took these criticisms head-on and doubled down. Emily’s outfits weren’t meant to be couture or designer; they were meant to dress a girl finding her sense of self, expressing her desire to explore the unknown.

For six seasons, Fitoussi curated a wardrobe fit for Emily, a bright-eyed young woman unafraid to try something new, to break the rules. This mirrors Fitoussi’s personal philosophy on clothing: that fashion is meant to break rules, to push boundaries, to provide a space of unrelenting experimentation. Ahead of the sixth season, SCAD FASH Museum of Fashion + Film compiles six seasons’ worth of outfits in “Emily in Paris: Fashion Without Rules,” on view through March 14, 2027. The exhibition lives up to its name; for the designer, clothing is a mode of expression that lets anyone feel free, wherever they are. It offers a character study, tracing Emily’s evolution from a doe-eyed expat to a well-versed Parisian resident. (And worry not, there are also looks from Emily’s chic boss Sylvie—played with devastating elegance by Philippine Leroy-Beaulieu.)

Ahead of season 6, Bazaar sat down with Fitoussi at SCAD Fashion in Atlanta to discuss working with Lily Collins, her swan song for Emily in Paris, and how everyone has the potential for creativity.

Marylin Fitoussi: I don’t recall a contemporary TV show being in the spotlight in this way. Generally, when you think of an exhibition, you think of period pieces or couture pieces. The show is really part of pop culture now!

MF: I was surprised when fashion magazines [criticized the show] at the beginning. I’m not a fashion designer, [but] I love fashion and I love clothes. This show was not about fashion at the beginning. [Emily] is a bubbly character with a very strong personality from Chicago; she couldn’t have come dressed in Comme des Garçons or in Yamamoto. I needed to have this cultural shock. She’s a fish-out-of-water character, and we needed something to catch the audience’s eyes. When you want to show people that you love the culture but you can’t express it because you don’t know the codes, you don’t speak the language, the only way you find it is through clothes. It was never about “fashion.” Sometimes, it’s about creativity, individuality, making something not trendy at all. The audience got that, and fashion magazines didn’t get it, so they killed me.

MF: Many times, I’ve asked myself, “Why does this little gingham suit have so much influence?” It’s quite simple. It was the most duplicated, copied, reposted, fan-arted, and used as a Halloween costume. It touched people because it was for them. The French can have their own version of it, their own concept, but for the entire world, it was this one little girly, timeless outfit with the red beret, the red lips, the red soul.

MF: She read the bad press after the release of season 1, and we had a talk. I said they hated it in France; they find it hideous. [I asked her] “Do you want me to change [it]?” She was smiling and said, “No, we can’t, and we won’t please everybody. We need to keep this strong DNA. We need to continue to have this unexpected silhouette because it’s what catches the audience’s eye.” It’s a guilty pleasure. We can say, I love it.

It opens a way for the audience to see fashion in a different way, where you can mix in an awkward way and free people from this law where you shouldn’t [do that]. Coco Chanel used to say, “Before leaving a room, look at yourself in the mirror and take something out.” I always say, “Put something more on.”

MF: I wanted to present a more elevated version, more mature, more evolved, but still true to what she was and what she is, with an eclectic combination and a little bit awkward. She knows the French rules, but as I do, she finds French fashion so boring. In general, I find that fashion is less and less interesting. Why are fashion and celebrity stylists sourcing more and more from archives? What it’s showing is that now everything is the same. Everything is boring, and I understand why. They need to sell the show! We don’t have to sell anything. We have to sell dreams, illusions, craziness, boldness. People watch the show in groups. Some people say, “I love it,” and some say, “I hate it,” and they have a dialogue and fight and have a good [time]. We love that.

MF: A young designer wants to be famous right away. Fame doesn’t happen, and it doesn’t matter. You need to be happy with what you’re doing. With costume design versus fashion design, you can be much freer. You don’t have anything to sell, and you don’t have to design the “It bag.” If your show is successful, it’s a win-win for everybody. To see that, you need to be true to your vision. You need to be true to your gut feeling, to your vision, to your DNA. Talent is not enough; you need to be at the right place at the right time. Being discovered by Darren Star … he changed my life. At some point, you find the right project for you.

You need to work a lot to take care of every detail. You need to be strong and push the boundaries. You need to try to show a different way to see costumes and clothes, to see that everything is possible…. Style begins when fear ends. You don’t want to please everybody, and I’m always attracted to people who dress in a different way, and I’m never judgmental. To create something is to expose yourself. It’s very vulnerable. It’s brave.

This interview has been condensed and edited for clarity.

#6737. Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando Are Married

Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando have officially tied the knot. Entertainment Tonight reported that they got married in Palm Springs on November 21.

Few details about their wedding have emerged, which isn’t surprising given that the couple kept most of the planning private. In March 2026, a source told People that they weren’t interested in having a big wedding—instead, they were envisioning a “smaller and meaningful” celebration.

Cyrus had “ideas” about what she’d like, “but she’s not planning some huge, traditional event,” the source added. “Maxx is extremely private, and that’s just not who he is. When they do get married, it will be something smaller and meaningful to them. Not a big Hollywood production.”

In July, Morando spoke to Wonderland about how he first met Cyrus in 2021. “Sam in my band [Liily], his sister’s friend knew Miley,” he said. “They just put us on a blind date. Which, from Miley’s perspective, I don’t think is really possible, because she’s so in the public eye. So it felt like if there was a way to have a blind date for her, this might be the most blind date that she could do.”

They connected during the date and “just never stopped hanging out,” he said.

It took Morando some time to adjust to the attention Cyrus receives. “When I first met her, that part of it was strange,” he said. “I’ve never experienced people waiting outside places for you and things like that. #6736. 27 Charming Christmas Towns That Look Like a Real-Life Holiday Movie

Think twinkling lights, towering trees, and Santa-themed bike rides.

The holiday season is in full swing, with many halls and houses already decked to impress in garland and fairy lights. But as you wrap gifts, prepare to host, and begin marathoning holiday movies, it can feel like the joyous season is coming to an end much too soon. We can't blame you if you're still wanting more from this merry time of year, and we've come up with a solution. There are plenty of beautiful Christmas towns across the country to fill your heart with peace, joy, and nostalgia—you just have to know where to look.

These towns are more than just beautifully decorated—they’re truly immersive, offering experiences from Santa-themed bike rides to orchestrated light shows and winter bar crawls. Below, we've rounded up the 27 most charming Christmas towns from all over the country, so no matter where you live, you'll be close enough to find a bit of extra cheer this year.

This picturesque mountain town serves as the perfect holiday backdrop for more reasons than just the ever-present blanket of fluffy white snow. Each year, the valley is transformed into a Christmas town with seasonal theatrical performances, Gunnison’s Night of Lights, a tree lighting ceremony, and even an ice sculpting event.

Ever since the formation of this city on Christmas Eve in 1741, Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, has been rooted in the holiday spirit. From Christmas markets to historical tours to horse-drawn carriage rides, there's no doubt this town won't feel magical. And make sure to stop by the historic Sayre Mansion, pictured here, to check out their elegant holiday decor.

Annapolis is known as one of the best cities during the holiday season thanks to its winter weather and historic downtown. If you're lucky enough to visit this Christmas town, make sure you spend time bargain shopping until midnight, checking out the spectacular light display in Sandy Point State Park, and viewing the Yacht Club Light Parade.

Chicago is exceptionally beautiful during the Christmas time. From the seemingly endless strings of lights to the Christkindlmarket, which is free to enter and so charming, the Windy City has many offerings during the holiday season, making it one of the best Christmas towns to visit. Plus, you don't want to miss ice skating or any Christmas-themed museum exhibits.

If you want to do something Christmas-y almost every single day of December, then Newport, Rhode Island, might just be the place to go. To create the perfect coastal Christmas, this town offers a month-long celebration that's been going strong for 54 years. From holiday bike rides to Medieval festivals to winter afternoon teas, there's so much to do in this Christmas town.

You'll feel as if you've traveled back to Charles Dickens's time when you walk through Franklin's historic Christmas festival. Characters from A Christmas Carol and Oliver Twist come to life throughout the weekend-long festivities. Roam the Victorian Village and try Victorian-era Christmas treats like sugar plums while listening to carolers.

A classic ski town, Park City offers Christmas markets, festive decorations, and a Christmas Eve parade lit by torches—plus spectacular views of the mountains are around every corner.

In the heart of Virginia horse country, you'll find one of the most festive Christmas towns. Cheer on the town's hunting hounds while sipping hard cider and wander the streets in search of vintage Christmas ornaments.

During Kennebunkport's annual Christmas Prelude, the town puts on a very New England celebration: You can watch Santa Claus arrive by lobster boat, go on seashore holiday trolley rides, and enjoy wine tastings and lobster bakes. Not to mention, the town is covered in Christmas lights and garlands that make it the perfect festive photo backdrop.

For a dreamy and unique experience, head to Santa Fe. One of the most anticipated celebrations is the Canyon Road Farolito Walk, which is when thousands of farolitos—luminaries made of paper bags, sand, and tea candles—cast a glow on the gardens and old buildings that line the road. You also can get your white Christmas fix by visiting Ski Santa Fe.

As one of the oldest towns in the country, Portsmouth is a charming New England destination that celebrates the holidays with a Vintage Christmas Celebration. Visit the historic village of Strawberry Banke or wander around the charming shopping districts in this historic Christmas town.

Get a Hallmark movie feel while experiencing a taste of Denmark in California's Solvang village, located in Santa Ynez Valley wine country. The destination hosts Julefest, a month-long holiday celebration with live entertainment, a parade, and a night market.

Koziar's Christmas Village in Bernville is one of the top attractions in Pennsylvania. With more than a million lights adorning buildings, barns, and the landscape—and a reflective lake that doubles the beauty—it's hard to beat the town's display.

This Bavarian-style village is charming any time of year! December festivities include a display of Santa costumes from all around the world, a gingerbread house competition, carolers, and plenty of photo ops.

Of course, New York City isn't a small Christmas town, but it is extra magical during the holidays. From the massive tree at Rockefeller Center to the various Christmas markets in the city parks with ice skating, shops, and more, you can't beat the Big Apple's holiday spirit.

Nicknamed the Lighted Poinsettia Capital of Texas, this town brings major holiday spirit every year. Visit during December when the lighted trail in Comanche Trail Park is aglow all month long. Check out Hotel Settles for its elegant Art Deco lodging.

During the holiday season, each home in Historic Williamsburg lights one candle, a tradition that dates back to the Revolutionary War era. The cobblestone streets and colonial holiday traditions such as caroling by torchlight make this destination a must, especially for history buffs.

This Christmas town stays decked out year-round, so if you're craving holiday spirit in July, you'll still find candy-cane posts, boughs of holly, and a Santa Claus house with live reindeer!

Christmas without the cold? We've got you covered! In addition to abundant sunshine and festive holiday decor, you'll also have plenty of history to explore in St. Augustine, America's oldest city.

Want to take a ride on the Polar Express? Visit Durango during the holidays. The historic mining town offers a Polar Express–inspired trip that your kiddos will flip over.

After briefly dating in 2012 (side note: Jai accused Ari of cheating with Nathan Sykes, which she denied), these two got back together in 2014 only to break up again.

Ariana dated The Wanted’s Nathan Sykes in 2013—around the time their song “Almost Is Never Enough” (which I definitely still fully listen to on repeat) debuted.

According to People, Ariana confirmed their split in January 2014, saying they ended things because of distance. The ’ship doesn’t appear to have made too much of a lasting impression on Ariana, because Nathan was not name-dropped in “thank u, next,” which he told TMZ was “good.”

Meanwhile, a source told Us Weekly, “They made the decision to part ways because their conflicting touring schedules would keep them apart over the next year.”

And, yes, for all of you wondering, Big Sean was indeed name-checked on “thank u, next,” when Ariana sang, “Thought I’d end up with Sean / But he wasn’t a match.”

Ricky and Ariana dated during her aforementioned Doughnut Debacle and got close when he was working as one of her backup dancers. A source told E! News re: their split, “She broke up with him. P.S. Here’s Ricky reacting to the “thank u, next” lyrics “Wrote some songs about Ricky / Now I listen and laugh.”

Ariana and Mac Miller dated for two years before parting ways in May 2018.

After Mac’s tragic death in September 2018, Ariana told Vogue in 2019 that “by no means was what we had perfect. He was the best person ever, and he didn’t deserve the demons he had. It was all a lot! But after a fast-moving few months that included an engagement, Pete and Ariana parted ways in October 2019.

A month later, he told Paper magazine, “I don’t ever make public statements about relationships ’cause I just don’t think it’s right, you know? But it was short-lived, and they ended things in early 2020—before Ariana started seeing Dalton Gomez. Which brings us to...

Ariana and Dalton got together right around the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, and by December 2020, they were engaged. The two then tied the knot in May 2021 at her Montecito home, and all seemed to be going well...until just about two years later, when their split was announced.

TMZ broke the news that Ariana and Dalton had been separated since January 2023 and were “heading toward divorce” in July 2023, with sources saying distance (at the time, Ariana had been in England filming Wicked) played a big part. In September 2023, the couple officially filed for divorce.

Which brings us back to Ricky! Soon after the Ethan breakup news dropped, Ari started quietly changing the Ricky lyrics in “thank u, next” during her Eternal Sunshine Tour. Several sightings of the two together followed until, eventually, the couple showed up at the Focker-In-Law premiere together, making clear they are very much back on.

#6734. Why Don’t You … Take Fashion Inspiration from the World’s Great Performers?

Diana Vreeland had a singular take on not only fashion but life. Her eccentricity has become folklore and was best exemplified in an illustrated column of irreverent advice for chic living she called “Why Don’t You?” Resurrected and reimagined for modern life, the column, now written by Bazaar’s executive digital director, Lynette Nylander, will dispense tips on how to live stylishly, decadently, and daringly.

Here’s a thought: Don’t get dressed. Mount a production. Put on a show. Go on tour. And if the reviews are lukewarm, don’t change the costume; blame the critic! For the performance issue, Lynette Nylander takes cues from the stage’s most stylish to arm you with tips for stepping out.

that the “effortless” look took 40 minutes. The “I just threw it on” leather jacket, the smudged eye makeup, the shirt that looks slept in: All of it is stagecraft. Miley Cyrus’s new rock-star look personifies this. She’s not someone to shy away from an “era,” and this one is all tousled hair, loads of lashes, and leather and lace from the likes of Tom Ford, Roberto Cavalli, and Saint Laurent. Effortless? No. Fabulous? Absolutely!

some noise. Taffeta rustles, silk whispers, embellishments jangle, and leather creaks with intent. Performance is not only visual. The swish of a skirt on a staircase is part of the entrance, and the weight of crepe hugging the hips is part of the walk. The late, great Tina Turner was a master of clothes that created a symphony as she writhed around the stage; often, they were the creations of the late, great Bob Mackie. Björk went viral earlier this year at the Venice Biennale in a neon-pink Bottega Veneta dress made of fiberglass shards that jingle-jangled together as she fist-pumped. The lesson? Dress for the ear as well as the eye.

the precision of a uniform. The chef’s whites, the lawyer’s suit, the professor’s tweeds, the tailored black of the gallery assistant: Each is a costume designed with a very particular audience in mind. Even people who wear the same thing every day are making a statement, and the strongest of them curate that repetition with real rigor. Consistency, done well, is a kind of theater. Just don’t make it boring! Consider Steve Jobs, who famously wore only Issey Miyake turtlenecks and Levi’s. Truly the only tech titan to ever have taste!

the art of quick change. For Céline Dion’s fall residency at the Plénitude Arena in Paris, underneath the spotlight wasn’t the only site where a performance took place. Like all true divas, Dion knows that every moment of every day is an opportunity to perform. Outside of the Royal Monceau hotel, her home in Paris, where her faithful fans lined up to greet her, she treated onlookers to a dance, a song, an air-kiss, and always a fashion show: off-the-runway looks from Jacquemus, Loewe, and Phoebe Philo. As they say, all the world’s a stage.

the ordinary garment its moment. Not every act needs sequins. A perfect white tee, a pair of jeans that have taken on the shape of a life, a forever leather jacket worn with confidence: these are the understudies who steal the show. Performance in fashion is not always about drama. Sometimes it is the quiet authority of a simple thing worn exactly right. A disciple of this way of dressing? Kim Gordon, whose effortless style, both onstage and offstage, has made her your favorite celebrity’s favorite celebrity for the past 40 years.

#6730. This Wood Finish Was Once Seen as “Outdated.” But Designers Now Say It's Coming Back.

You might regret ripping out those kitchen cabinets.

For a period of time in the late 1980s to early 2000s, it seemed virtually impossible to enter a house and not come across honey oak. That bright, orange-toned wood finish covered kitchen cabinets, bathroom vanities, even baseboard trim and furniture around the house.

“You’d see it everywhere—cabinetry, trim, stair railings, and floors. It was the go-to wood tone for builders and homeowners alike,” Cathleen Gruver of Gruver Cooley tells House Beautiful. “But by the early 2000s, it started to fall out of favor as people shifted toward cooler, more neutral interiors.”

However, there’s been a noticeable shift in the way people are wanting their interiors to look, and warmer spaces are definitely back in style. With this evolution, can we expect to see a revival of honey oak, as well? We asked a handful of designers if they think this golden wood finish is back, and how they would style it for modern-day interiors.

Elizabeth Bennett and Mallory Robins, the founders of interior design studio Kobel + Co, believe honey oak is back for two reasons: The first is that warm tones throughout the entirety of the home are on the rise; the second is that honey oak has a lot of nostalgic associations for people who grew up in the '80s and '90s and are now homeowners.

“We're seeing a resurgence of styles from this era not only in homes, but in fashion as well, as we harken back to a pre-digital era,” Bennett explains.

“It’s not necessarily a full-blown comeback, but I’ve definitely noticed a soft return—particularly in cabinetry, millwork details, and furniture," Gruver says. “Clients aren’t always asking for 'honey oak' by name, but they are gravitating toward natural wood tones that offer warmth and character.”

Before you take a sledgehammer to those original honey oak cabinets, reconsider this tone by styling it in more modern ways. Keep reading to see fresh ways that designers are working with honey oak in their new projects.

As homeowners gravitate more toward lived-in, inviting interiors, honey oak is a wonderful way to add warmth. Leave it to the professionals to find stylish ways to make this once-outdated wood tone look cool again.

Plenty of designers will tell you to mix wood tones in your home to prevent it from feeling one-note, and the same is encouraged when honey oak makes a big presence. When designer Adina Hall took on the project above, there was too much honey oak in the space for her team to replace or refinish it all, so they embraced it instead.

“We developed a custom stain for the new wood floors, a whitewashed French oak that created a neutral canvas for the structure without competing with the existing honey tone,” Hall says. “We added custom cabinetry finished in a taupe-tone ash veneer, again a neutral tone, and we leaned into crisp whites and some cool tones like sage green and indigo blue as accents to create a balanced palette.”

Heavy amounts of warm woods can overwhelm the eye; it’s important to build a restrained palette and introduce interest with cooler tones, wood stains, sculptural furniture, and contrasting materials. “The key is to give the honey oak a contemporary context in order to make it feel like an intentional material that delivers a punch of warmth in an otherwise cool and architecturally bold yet restrained palette.”

Whether you’re adding in fresh honey oak or you’re trying to work around what’s already in your home, one of the best ways to ensure it feels modern and not like a ‘90s Tuscan-inspired home is choosing an earthy color palette. Muted greens, warm whites, greiges, taupe, light blues—these are all beautiful hues that won’t add even more orange-ish warmth to your space.

“Instead of making honey oak the focus of the room, I let the beauty of the wood shine through the use of clean lines, black matte touches, natural stones, and modern lighting,” designer Nancy Dow of Sierra Living Concepts says. She’s fond of using this wood, and uses these shades to create a modern and fresh appearance.

Rather than “wood drenching” a home in a single tone (as was often seen in the early aughts), Robins explains that current homeowners are exercising more restraint with their finishes. “Rather than the primary finish for a house on trim, floors, and cabinetry, it's being used in more subtle ways—a cased good piece or a kitchen island alone,” she says.

One of the reasons honey oak fell out of style is because it is a very warm tone, and in the world of “millennial gray,” an orange-tinted kitchen or bathroom isn’t very appealing. However, designer Marli Jones of Rebel House design studio believes this can be fixed simply by creating a contrasting palette.

In the kitchen space above, Jones used only honey oak cabinetry in the scullery to contrast the light, bright main kitchen. “It adds a coziness to the scullery and envelops the space in warm, natural tones,” she says. “That same honey color travels across the countertop stone and into the tile backsplash.” The two rooms are connected by the wall of glass and steel, but the change in materiality from the white cabinets to the honey oak creates a dynamic transition. “Warm wood always adds a grounding layer.”

When adding a honey oak piece into your home, do so intentionally. Opt for a “stunning built-in, a custom island, or as an accent detail that brings texture and warmth,” Gruver says. To emphasize the styling, pair the honey oak piece with contemporary hardware or painted elements to help it feel fresh and curated.

While honey oak can work in any interior aesthetic, there are a few styles it looks best in, according to Gruver: updated farmhouse and cottagecore. Basically, “any space that leans into character, craft, and comfort,” she explains. However, she's also seen the tone used successfully in more modern, organic spaces where there's a large emphasis on natural materials and textures. It all depends on how it's balanced, which holds true for any wood tone. She adds, “When styled right, honey oak can absolutely feel current again.”

Follow House Beautiful on Instagram and TikTok.

#6729. The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’s Cast Is Totally Stacked

See Joseph Zada, Whitney Peak, Elle Fanning, Kieran Culkin, Jesse Plemons, and Glenn Close in the new movie

The Hunger Games franchise is welcoming a new installment, Sunrise on the Reaping, the sixth film adaptation of Suzanne Collins’s best-selling dystopian saga.

Releasing on November 20, the film boasts a star-studded cast of about 33 actors and counting, poised to bring a blend of familiar names and new faces to the world of Panem.

Ahead of the film, we’re reacquainting ourselves with beloved characters from the original trilogy, like Effie Trinket (Elle Fanning), Caesar Flickerman (Kieran Culkin), Beetee (Kelvin Harrison Jr.), and Wiress (Maya Hawke). Even the completely new characters, like Maysilee Donner and Lenore Dove, have family ties to well-known characters in the franchise.

Based on Collins’s second prequel novel, Sunrise on the Reaping delves into the brutal 50th Hunger Games, spotlighting a young Haymitch Abernathy 24 years before he became Katniss and Peeta’s mentor. We, as readers, thought we knew a detailed account of the second Quarter Quell from Mockingjay, but as we learn in the Sunrise on the Reaping novel, much of what we learned was manipulated by the Capitol to be used as propaganda.

This much is still true: With twice the tributes, the 50th Hunger Games doubles the bloodshed, trauma, and size of the cast. To prepare for the inevitably heart-wrenching film, get to know the extensive cast.

Joseph Zada is a 21-year-old Australian actor best known for playing Johnny Sinclair in the television series We Were Liars and Cal Trask in East of Eden.

Zada shows a very different side of Woody Harrelson’s character, before the biting sarcasm and heavy drinking. In the new film, we follow 16-year-old Haymitch’s harrowing journey through the 50th Hunger Games and, arguably, a more distressing journey after victory. We knew Zada was perfect for the role when he discussed re-creating Harrelson’s Mockingjay Part 2 red-carpet pajama moment.

Elle Fanning is a 28-year-old American actress best known for her roles as Aurora in Maleficent, Syvie Russo in A Complete Unknown, and Catherine in The Great, as well as being half of an iconic sister duo with Dakota Fanning.

While Trinket is only a side character in Sunrise on the Reaping, her casting was one of the most highly anticipated, with fans almost unanimously agreeing that Fanning was the only correct choice to reprise Elizabeth Banks’s character. In Sunrise on the Reaping, Trinket is a young member of the Capitol styling and beauty team for District 12.

It’s possible that Suzanne Collins got tired of the endless Coriolanus Snow thirst edits on TikTok and went ahead and cast Voldemort. No, really, 63-year-old English actor Ralph Fiennes is best known for his role as Voldemort in the Harry Potter film series.

Fiennes plays President Snow, a younger version of the late Donald Sutherland’s character in the original trilogy and an older version of Tom Blythe’s character in The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes. President Snow reaches his peak level of viciousness in Sunrise on the Reaping, and Fiennes is the perfect vessel to carry out Snow’s evil plans.

Kieran Culkin is a 44-year-old actor best known for his roles in A Real Pain and Succession. Despite recently winning an Oscar, Emmy, Golden Globe, and SAG Award, his brother Macaulay still has him beat in household name recognition for his childhood role in Home Alone. Reprising Stanley Tucci's role as Hunger Games host Caesar Flickerman may change that.

Jesse Plemons is a 38-year-old actor best known for his roles in Friday Night Lights and Breaking Bad (and for being married to Kirsten Dunst). In another impeccable casting choice, Plemons also played the son of the original Plutarch (the late Philip Seymour Hoffman) in The Master (2012).

In both Sunrise on the Reaping and the original trilogy, Plutarch Heavensbee is an old-money Capitol citizen whose morally gray philosophies make him one of the franchise’s most fascinating characters. In the new film, we see him as a young, ambitious cameraman, years before he became head gamemaker.

Lili Taylor is a 59-year-old American actress and author best known for her roles in Mystic Pizza and The Conjuring. She has the perfect sweet smile to play Mags Flanagan, the victor of the 11th Hunger Games from District 4.

Mags, previously played by the late Lynn Cohen, was introduced in Catching Fire when she volunteered to take Annie Cresta's place in the 75th Hunger Games. In Sunrise on the Reaping, Mags acts as District 12's mentor, as they have no surviving winners of their own.

Maya Hawke is the 28-year-old daughter of Uma Thurman and Ethan Hawke, best known for her roles as Robin in Stranger Things and Anxiety in Inside Out 2.

She plays Wiress, the District 3 victor fresh out of the 49th Hunger Games. Amanda Plummer played the character in Catching Fire, when she was reaped with Beetee as the 75th Hunger Games District 3 tributes.

Kelvin Harrison Jr. is a 32-year-old actor who previously played the son of the original Beetee (Jeffrey Wright) in Monsters (2018).

As the Hunger Games fan account Panem Propaganda said, “If I had a nickel for every time a Sunrise on the Reaping cast member played the son of their older Hunger Games counterpart in a completely unrelated movie, I’d have two nickels. Which isn’t a lot, but it’s weird that it happened twice,” referring to the castings of Beetee and Plutarch.

Beetee was the winner of the 34th Hunger Games from District 3 who was reaped for the 75th Hunger Games in Catching Fire. The new film delves into his heartbreaking backstory, involving the fate of his son, Ampert, as well as his secret plan with Haymitch to disrupt the games.

Iris Apatow is a 24-year-old actress who previously appeared in This Is 40, The Bubble, and Knocked Up. She is the daughter of actress Leslie Mann and producer Judd Apatow, the sister of Euphoria star Maude Apatow, and the girlfriend of White Lotus star Sam Nivola. She plays Proserpina Trinket, Effie’s younger sister and member of the District 12 prep team.

Edvin Ryding is a 23-year-old Swedish actor who previously appeared in 28 Years Later and Young Royals. He plays Vitus, Proserpina’s friend and sidekick on the District 12 prep team.

Whitney Peak is a 23-year-old Ugandan-Canadian actress best known for her role as Zoya in the 2021 Gossip Girl reboot. She plays Lenore Dove, the Covey singer and love of Haymitch's life.

Though her character is unique to Sunrise on the Reaping, Lenore Dove is rumored to be the daughter of either Maude Ivory or Lucy Gray Baird. Fans can’t help but notice the resemblance between Peak and Rachel Zegler.

McKenna Grace is a 20-year-old actress best known for her roles in The Handmaid's Tale, Ghostbusters: Afterlife, and Young Sheldon. While young, she has been acting since she was five, and she has had at least 34 film and television roles.

She plays Maysilee Donner, the spoiled mean girl who turns into a star when she is reaped for the 50th Hunger Games. She has a twin sister, Merrilee (whose daughter later gifts Katniss the Mockingjay pin), and is friends with Asterid March, Katniss's mother. She allies herself with Haymitch during the game, and the two share a sibling-like bond.

Ben Wang is a 29-year-old actor best known for his roles in Karate Kid: Legends and American Born Chinese.

He plays Wyatt Callow, Haymitch's fellow District 12 boy tribute. The Callow family runs the gambling scene in District 12, placing bets on the Hunger Games tributes each year.

Wang’s Instagram is @definitelynotbenwang.

Glenn Close is a 79-year-old Tony, Emmy, and Golden Globe winner best known for her roles in Fatal Attraction, 101 Dalmatians, and The Deliverance.

She plays Drusilla Sickle, the District 12 tributes’ escort. Drusilla is known for her many cosmetic surgeries that poorly attempt to disguise her age. She and Maysilee are the biggest divas in Panem, and their personalities clash disastrously.

Billy Porter is a 57-year-old Emmy, Tony, and Grammy Award–winning actor, singer, composer, director, and playwright.

He plays Magno Stift, the incompetent stylist for the District 12 tributes. His personal style involves wearing a plethora of live reptiles, and his hobbies include licking frogs for the psychedelic effects.

Molly McCann is a young Irish actress who previously appeared in Bad Sisters, Herself, and Rosie. She plays Louella McCoy, a young girl from District 12 who Haymitch views as a little sister and nicknamed “Sweetheart.” Fans were quick to notice McCann's resemblance to Katniss (Jennifer Laurence), the only other character who Haymitch refers to as Sweetheart.

McCann’s Instagram is @mollymccannactress.

Iona Bell is a young English actress who plays Louella’s uncanny lookalike, Lou Lou.

Her Instagram is @iona_bell_official_actor.

Kara Tointon is a 43-year-old English actress who previously appeared in EastEnders, The Teacher, and Too Good to Be True. She plays Willamae Abernathy, Haymitch's mother.

#6728. All About Maxx Morando, Miley Cyrus’s Husband

Miley Cyrus and Liily drummer Maxx Morando are officially married. The couple tied the knot in Palm Springs, California, on November 21, nearly five years after they were first romantically linked. The ceremony took place poolside beneath an arch of white flowers, with Cyrus’s mother, Tish Cyrus, and sister Noah Cyrus among those in attendance.

Dating rumors linking the two musicians first bubbled up at the end of 2021, after they were seen together in Miami while Cyrus was in town for her New Year’s Eve special, Miley’s New Year’s Eve Party for NBC.

There were also glimpses of them dancing backstage. Months later, in March 2022, Entertainment Tonight confirmed the two were together, with a source calling their relationship “low-key.”

The couple enjoyed their love story in private and ultimately made their awards show debut at the Oscars in March 2025. That December, they announced their engagement.

Here’s what we know about Maxx Morando and their romance’s history.

Before joining the four-person Los Angeles rock band Liily, Morando played drums for the punk rock band The Regrettes from 2015 to 2018, and he even performed on Conan in 2017. He and Cyrus have many mutual friends and have known one another as friends for a while.

Cyrus and Morando were together on the red carpet at the Gucci Love Parade fashion show in Los Angeles in November 2021. But a source confirmed their relationship to E! in January 2022. “She’s happily dating Maxx,” said the insider. “It’s official between them.”

The source added, “They are both artistic and creative, so they bond over being musicians,” and confirmed Morando joined her at the NYE party. “He was backstage with Miley and Pete [Davidson] at the New Year’s Eve rehearsals and taping having a good time with them. They were are all super friendly with one another and seemed to have a great night.”

Entertainment Tonight added in a report published on March 1, 2022, that the two have been together privately for some time.

“Miley and Maxx have been having a good time together,” the source said. “They’ve been together for a little while and are just enjoying their relationship. Miley likes the fact that they are low-key as a couple and is just focused on doing her thing and being around people that make her happy, and Maxx does that.”

Then, on April 14, 2022, the couple was photographed kissing in West Hollywood, further confirming the relationship. They then walked down the street shoulder-to-shoulder.

Nearly a year later, in March 2023, Cyrus and Morando confirmed they were still happily together. They made a joint appearance, holding hands, at the Versace show in Los Angeles hours before she dropped her album Endless Summer Vacation. Later that night, they celebrated the new release together at a Gucci party.

In September 2021, Cyrus mentioned Morando while talking to Vogue about her performance looks, attributing a print of cartoon monsters to the drummer, which he collaborated on with designer Shane Kastl.

“This look is a one-of-a-kind collaboration between two of my favorite emerging artists, Maxx Morando and Shane Kastl,” she said. “Their collaboration is the perfect example of sustainability becoming the next fashion phase, and it proves that anything can be reinvented, which resonates with me deeply.”

Cyrus also debuted a new song on NYE 2021 called “You,” which she said was so new she didn’t have a chance to record it yet. It later ended up as a track on her 2023 album Endless Summer Vacation. It’s been speculated that it’s about her new boyfriend. The lyrics go:

“I got some baggage / Let’s do some damage / I am not made for no horsey and carriage / You know I’m savage / You’re looking past it / I want that late night sweet magic / That forever lasting love / But only if it’s with you.”

In October 2022, a source told E! News that “Miley and Maxx are still going strong and their relationship is very serious...They have been together for about a year now, and Miley is really happy.”

They added, “Everyone in her family loves them together and thinks they mesh really well.”

Cyrus had apparently sold her home in Franklin, Tennessee, and moved to Los Angeles, the source said, explaining, “She wanted to take a step back from a crazy work schedule recently. She’s in a good place.”

Years later, on May 9, 2025, Billy Ray Cyrus shared a selfie featuring his daughter and his son Braison to celebrate the latter’s 31st birthday. Morando also made an appearance in the photo, being hugged by Miley.

A Cyrus source told People in March 2023 that Morando is a “cool guy,” and the lack of drama attached to him has been really nice for Cyrus.

“He has no interest in being a huge celebrity; he’s very low-key. Miley loves these qualities,” the source said. “Miley can be herself. They are supportive of each other’s careers. Miley is enjoying life and things are great.”

Believe it or not, it’s true. Cyrus told British Vogue, “Well, it was blind for me and not really for him,” she clarified. “I thought, ‘The worst that can happen is I leave.’” Luckily, it turned out much better than that.

Another fun tidbit: His ringtone on her phone is “Tyrone” by Erykah Badu. “I call that ‘boyfriend sexy ringtone’,” she told the mag. Usually, though, Morando is the one with the phone. When Endless Summer Vacation was released, Cyrus didn’t have hers on her. “My boyfriend brings his phone, and I don’t bring one,” she said.

Cyrus was spotted out at a concert that Morando’s band Liily played on Oct. 11, 2023, in Los Angeles. Photos of her with brown hair alongside Morando surfaced on X.

On Feb. 4, 2024, the couple attended the Grammys together.

The couple was caught on camera having a very intimate moment at Cyrus’s Grammys table. While they didn’t walk the red carpet together, Morando joined her inside the ceremony. Cyrus won her first two Grammys that night and performed onstage.

A source told People in a Feb. 7, 2024, report that Cyrus and Morando had moved in together. “She is very happy with him,” the source said. “Miley has changed a lot in the past couple of years. She seems more calm and harmonious. Everyone loves Maxx. He’s a great guy. She is very happy with him. He’s private and doesn’t like being in the press. It’s been good for her.”

On Saturday, August 31, Cyrus attended Morando’s concert in West Hollywood at the Roxy. She was photographed heading out to her car in a tight black T-shirt and Gucci sunglasses. She had her hair back in a tight bun.

Cyrus and Morando enjoyed a Future Islands concert at the Shrine Auditorium in Los Angeles. Photos came out of their rare date night on September 18. Cyrus wore an oversize black sweater, while Morando was in a navy Ralph Lauren Polo Bear sweater. See pics here.

The singer spoke to Harper’s Bazaar in November 2024, noting she notices a generation gap between them. Cyrus is a millennial while Morando is Gen Z.

“He looks at life really differently than I do,” she said. “He grew up with a laptop. I had a desktop computer that I shared with my brothers and sisters.…Honestly, he’s raised our dog off Reddit. I’m like, ‘Are you sure we’re supposed to be doing this?’ And he’s like, ‘On Reddit, it says blah, blah, blah.’”

“He’s very similar to me. We just don’t take life too seriously,” she added.

Cyrus revealed to Harper’s Bazaar in November 2024 that she and Morando have been collaborating musically. Working with a loved one is not out of the ordinary for her: “I worked with my dad forever,” she said. “That’s how me and my ex-husband [Liam Hemsworth] met each other. I’ve always worked with the people that I love. And Maxx just inspires me so much.”

On February 16, Cyrus and Morando walked the red carpet at SNL50, a celebration of Saturday Night Live’s 50th season. Cyrus performed at the live-streamed event and Morando was by her side.

The couple posed together on the red carpet.

Then, they attended the Vanity Fair Oscar Party. For both events, they matched in black ensembles.

Morando is the drummer in Cyrus’s “End of the World” video, which premiered in April 2025. His face is obscured, but he’s at the drum set during the entire video:

He also appears in a few other visuals for the album, which dropped in May 2025.

On Friday, June 6, they were seen at Hotel Beacon in New York City after she premiered her visual album, Something Beautiful, on day three of the Tribeca Festival. Cyrus was wearing a strapless gold and mirrored dress with a pair of pointed-toe gold heels, carrying a black clutch in one hand. She held Morando’s hand in the other. He was in a black suit and a white button-down.

On Dec. 1, 2025, the couple made a rare public appearance at the Hollywood premiere of Avatar: Fire and Ash. They wore coordinating all-black ensembles as Cyrus flashed a diamond sparkler with a gold band on her left ring finger. The accessory sparked engagement rumors online, and the following day, People confirmed that Cyrus and Morando were engaged.

On Feb. 1, 2026, Cyrus and Morando walked the red carpet together at the Grammy Awards. The singer was nominated in the Pop Vocal Album category.

On March 17, a source told People that the couple is envisioning a more intimate celebration.

“Maxx is extremely private, and that’s just not who he is,” the source said. “When they do get married, it will be something smaller and meaningful to them. Not a big Hollywood production.”

The insider added, “Miley really loves her life right now. Everything just feels like it’s falling into place for her.”

Cyrus and Morando also made a joint appearance in Los Angeles on March 24, stepping out together at the world premiere of the Hannah Montana 20th anniversary special.

On Friday, May 23, Cyrus was honored with a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame. Morando was by her side for the big event, where she wore vintage Atelier Versace. But her mother, Tish, may have revealed more than she intended when she referred to Morando as her daughter’s “husband.”

As Cyrus and her friends and family were posing for photographs, Tish reportedly referred to Morando by saying, “We’re gonna bring the husband.”

In an interview with Wonderland, Morando reflected on proposing to Cyrus during a trip to Japan, explaining that he deliberately waited until the end of their vacation to pop the question.

“We were in Kyoto, Japan,” he said. “For some reason—you’ll find this as crazy as I did—she’d never been to Japan before. Neither had I, and we’d both wanted to go for a really long time. There were talks before we went about me popping the question, but I was trying to keep it secret.”

He continued, “I had to be really sneaky about it. We went to Tokyo first for a couple days and then on to Kyoto. I think she had a sense that it was coming.”

Morando recalled proposing in a garden, saying, “It was a little dead end, this beautiful Japanese forest-y situation. She was taking videos and was turned away. That’s when I got on one knee and tapped her on the shoulder.”

He admitted he was nervous. “I was sweating,” he said. “I could feel my heart pounding. You grow up as a kid watching the movies where the guy gets on one knee and does the whole thing, and you know that’s what you’re supposed to do. But then you realize, ‘Okay, I literally have to get on one knee.’”

On September 1, Cyrus and Morando were photographed together during a casual outing in Los Angeles. Cyrus wore a dark brown sweatshirt with loose black pants and black flip-flops, carrying a black leather tote. Morando coordinated with her laid-back look in a fitted white tank top, dark green drawstring pants, and a brown baseball cap.

During a September 17 interview with Zane Lowe for Apple Music, Cyrus revealed that she suspected Morando might propose during their trip to Japan—and even searched him for a ring while they were out walking.

“Me and Maxx were actually going on a walk…and because I won’t allow anything to happen organically for this man, I was like, ‘Oh, I’m gonna pat him down. I bet he has an engagement ring. This would be the best time,’” she recalled. “I didn’t find it!”

Morando ultimately managed to surprise her. Cyrus recalled, “I turned around ‘cause I gasped and he was on one knee. He totally got away with it. He’s on the ground like, so sweet, and has a thing and says, ‘You’re the love of my life. Will you marry me?’ I was like, ‘Oh my God, I almost botched it.’ He was like, ‘So bad. You really almost truly ruined it.’”

Cyrus also reflected on what their relationship means to her now. “This part of my life is something I’ve always wanted, and this is what I hope other people get to have, what I have,” she said. “I don’t know if everybody gets to find their Maxx.”

On November 19, reports surfaced that Cyrus and Morando are planning to get married in Southern California over the weekend of November 21 to 22. The couple has not confirmed the news.

Cyrus and Morando got married in Palm Springs, California, on Saturday, November 21. They had a poolside ceremony that was officiated by the Flaming Lips frontman Wayne Coyne, a longtime friend of Cyrus’s.

The wedding was intimate. Months before, in March, a source told People that the couple wanted “something smaller and meaningful to them. Not a big Hollywood production.”
