#6663. 15 Best Zip-Up Hoodies for Men 2026, According to GQ Editors

Surveying the best zip-up hoodies for men takes me back to my younger days as a hopelessly romantic high school kid. My formative years were marred by angst, soundtracked by pop punk, emo, and indie rock. The piece of clothing that got me through it all? A zip-up hoodie. It was core to the indie aesthetic, with every forlorn frontman sporting one over a thrashed band tee, skinny jeans, and shredded Chucks. But nostalgia never seems to stay in the past, especially when fashion is involved.

Gen-Z has revived every minute piece of 2000s pop culture, which means zip-up hoodies are back and have all but usurped the pullover hoodie as the sweat du jour. The zip-up is inherently versatile in both practical wear and sheer styling dexterity. With the flick of the zip, you can put your beloved Death Cab for Cutie tee on full display while letting your pits breathe, or keep it zipped up when it's just a bit too nippy out. To find the best zip-up hoodies on the market, I dusted off Transatlanticism and went on a deep dive. The good news is that the old classics are still good. The better news is that there's a lot of great competition to choose from.

Uniqlo’s no-nonsense clean aesthetic and low price point has made it a go-to for any menswear enjoyer looking for good style on a budget. While the brand excels at cashmere sweaters, T-shirts, and a slew of homerun collabs, the Japanese label’s sweats are criminally underrated. We’d go so far as to say that they should be talked in the same breath as brands like Champion and Sunspel. This zip up hoodie took us by surprise thanks to its comfy midweight, all-cotton fabric and solid construction. But the main selling point is the impeccable fit.

So many other brands cut their hoodies too long in the body and leave you looking like Jack Skellington’s pubescent brother. Uniqlo managed to cut its French terry hoodie to sit right at the hips which makes for a more classic and natural silhouette that’s neither lanky nor sloppy. Because of the fabric, the feel, and the overall fit, this is my favorite zip-up hoodie by a sizable margin. It’s my most-worn hoodie and has yet to show signs of any fraying.

Hoodies were originally meant for sportswear, as warm up gear before a grueling game of football. These days, they’re more often worn for lounging on the couch to watch the kickoff. And if you want to kick it in comfort while saving your pennies for booze and amuse bouche for the big game with the boys, the best budget zip up hoodie to buy is Hanes’ EcoSmart zip hoodie. The fit is spot on—relaxed, but not sloppy, comfy in the body and the sleeves without swallowing you like a sand pit.

The fit is impressive for the price, and the overall quality means you’re getting a little more than what you pay for. It’s not a hoodie that’ll last you for too long, but it is a good quality piece for just 15 bucks. And when other hoodies offer lesser quality and worse-fitting options for about the same price? The answer is clear.

It’s hard not to sing the praises of Reigning Champ, a brand that built its fleece empire on sweatpants and hoodies. The Canadian label’s flagship midweight terry fabric has drawn the attention of streetwear royalty and menswear buffs alike and its dedication to quality has elevated the humble hoodie to oxygen-deprived heights. We named Reigning Champ’s crewneck sweatshirt and pullover hoodie as among our favorites in their respective categories, and the same goes for its zip-up hooded sweatshirt. It’s made of the same 100% cotton French terry fabric as its superlative-earning brethren and is cut with high-quality flatlock stitching for a smooth, un-bulky feel.

I had high expectations for Reigning Champ, given my previous experience, and I’m not surprised at all with how nice this zip-up is. And while I'm partial to the standard fit, it’s also available in a slim fit version, too.

Hoodies live in a universe well beyond the sportswear world from which they originated. And while we still enjoy the OGs and the classics that made the hoodie a bona fide menswear must-have, we also love seeing all the ways the style has been pushed, tweaked, and freaked. Our Legacy's Level Hood has been a successful avenue for the Stockholm-based brand to explore the limits of the hoodie and this particular version strikes a delicate balance between the freaky and the fashion-curious. It's made of an English wool knit into an all-over ribbed texture for a throwback '90s feel. The cropped, boxy silhouette and elongated sleeves harken back to the grunge-y era, while the sultry dual-tone nightshade colorway throws you off in the best way possible.

Menswear influencers will be happy to regale you with their TedTalk on the golden ratio of clothing proportions. Essentially, that means your outfit should be divided into three equal sections where the top takes up one third of the outfit. Basically, your tops should be cropped and sit closer to your natural waist. Follow it up with some high-waisted pants with a wide silhouette and you’ve instantly garnered 300K views on TikTok (RIP). With so many indie brands and influencers scrambling to make their own versions of “the perfect cropped hoodie” you’re probably tired of wading through all the choices. Do yourself a favor and go to Abercrombie.

The Moose’s version is backed by actual trend forecasters, actual designers, and actual fit models. What does that mean, exactly? It means that its cropped zip hoodie fits really well and uses surprisingly beefy fabric. It was a revelation for me, too—Abercrombie wasn’t a name I associated with hoodies, but after I saw this in person, I had to readjust my menswear word cloud.

Some of the best zip-up hoodies for men are made by a brand you never see in brick and mortar stores. Camber has been crafting the most durable sweats for decades, right here in America and have been the shining example of the difference between good quality and great quality. Sure, you have to order through an old-school web 1.0 website and wait for several weeks to actually get your hoodie. But trust us when we say that the relatively minor inconvenience is completely worth it.

The heavyweight fleece is almost as thick as a leather jacket and can stand in as outerwear if you wanted it to. While other hoodies are washed to hell in giant industrial washing machines to reach a super soft texture by the time it gets to you, Camber’s actually require you to do the work yourself. It sort of feels like you’re being swaddled by an anaconda, which means if you’re a proponent of hard clothes like raw denim, you’ll like Camber’s hoodie a lot.

Cashmere zip hoodies, once the exclusive province of Silicon Valley unicorn founders and PJ-flying nepo babies, have been democratized, none better than Naadam's take. You know the brand for bringing thoughtful, sustainable cashmere pieces at “really, only that much?” prices. Its zip hoodie is as soft as it gets, with extra credit points awarded for coming in a classic fit (too many cashmere hoodies err on the side of slim) and six colors, including this decidedly handsome olive. Wear it on weekends, work-from-home Fridays, and long flights—even if it's just Economy+.

Shoutout to brother in arms Louis Cheslaw, GQ Recs contributor, whose writing for the newsletter Magasin put us on to young brand Cease. From seed to sewing, it's beefy 20-ounce cotton is fully American-made. Assembling the fabric vertically means the hoodie will shorten up to a slightly cropped, oversized fit. Act fast if you want some of the less-boring colors—they move fast.

We can’t deny Russell Athletic’s contributions to the hoodie space. And while its formula has changed over the years, the new hoodies are still pretty good for the price. The fabric is soft and lightweight, and it’s available in a rainbow of colorways. Plus, if you’re looking for a hoodie with a little more length, this is a great option.

Bold graphics aren’t usually deemed classics, but Gap’s retro-leaning collegiate-style block logo has staying power almost as much as the Levi’s red tab. Add to that a wonderfully fluffy midweight fleece material and a tailored straight fit and you’ve got something you’ll see on moodboards for generations to come.

Champion’s Reverse Weave fabric is iconic for its nearly shrink-proof quality and almost unsettlingly rough exterior. Flip it to the inside and you’ve got a luxuriously brushed interior that’ll have you feeling like you’re melting into a cloud. Heads-up that pricing varies kinda wildly by size on Amazon.

The secondhand market is chock full of navy-blue hoodies that have been sun-faded and beaten down with time. They'll cost you just as much as this Mfpen version, but will also fall apart faster than you can zip 'em up.

Les Tien's dedication to all things sweats results in a catalog of luxurious fleece and terry cloth with a modern approach. Featuring high-end Cobrax hardware, RiRi zippers, raw-edge hems and sleeves, and a heavyweight brushed fleece, no detail is phoned in.

The Real McCoy's is considered by many to be Americana repro wizards. This revival of an early 20th-Century hoodie is just one small piece of the brand's preservation prowess. It's made using beefy sinker-knit fleece, old-school Talon-style zippers, and vertical patch pockets.

A.Presse's chokehold on the menswear illuminati refuses to let up and it's pieces like this vintage-inspired hoodie that keep the pressure on. Based on very rare “after-hood parkas", this made-in-Japan hoodie features an idiosyncratic attached hood, super dense and lofty fleece, with artfully distressed details throughout.

Think of the zip-up as the pullover hoodie's elder brother, but with way more layering potential. In its most natural state, it can cuddle up to a matching set of sweatpants and a baggy tee with flair. (Top it off with a swanky necklace, crisp sneakers, and some stellar shades and you’re left with a fit on par with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander at his tunnel-trotting best.)

Unzipped and left open, it can also take on the role of a picture frame ready to display your sickest graphic tee—much like the cardigan, another treasure of 2000s fashion. Or make like a mid-Aughts garage band ironically donning corporate attire and wear your zip-up over a dress shirt and baggy tailored trousers, a high-minded fashion move with a jolt of kooky Scandinavian cool.

Style is subjective, we know—that’s the fun of it. But we’re serious about helping our audience get dressed. Whether it’s the best white sneakers, the flyest affordable suits, or the need-to-know menswear drops of the week, GQ Recommends’ perspective is built on years of hands-on experience, an insider awareness of what’s in and what’s next, and a mission to find the best version of everything out there, at every price point.

Our staffers aren’t able to try on every single piece of clothing you read about on GQ.com (fashion moves fast these days), but we have an intimate knowledge of each brand’s strengths and know the hallmarks of quality clothing—from materials and sourcing, to craftsmanship, to sustainability efforts that aren’t just greenwashing. GQ Recommends heavily emphasizes our own editorial experience with those brands, how they make their clothes, and how those clothes have been reviewed by customers. Bottom line: GQ wouldn’t tell you to wear it if we wouldn’t.

We make every effort to cast as wide of a net as possible, with an eye on identifying the best options across three key categories: quality, fit, and price.

To kick off the process, we enlist the GQ Recommends braintrust to vote on our contenders. Some of the folks involved have worked in retail, slinging clothes to the masses; others have toiled for small-batch menswear labels; all spend way too much time thinking about what hangs in their closets.

We lean on that collective experience to guide our search, culling a mix of household names, indie favorites, and the artisanal imprints on the bleeding-edge of the genre. Then we narrow down the assortment to the picks that scored the highest across quality, fit, and price.

Across the majority of our buying guides, our team boasts firsthand experience with the bulk of our selects, but a handful are totally new to us. So after several months of intense debate, we tally the votes, collate the anecdotal evidence, and emerge with a list of what we believe to be the absolute best of the category right now, from the tried-and-true stalwarts to the modern disruptors, the affordable beaters to the wildly expensive (but wildly worth-it) designer riffs.

Whatever your preferences, whatever your style, there's bound to be a superlative version on this list for you. (Read more about GQ's testing process here.)

#6660. Olivia Dean Goes Backless in Straight-Off-the-Runway Conner Ives

The pop star brought a pop of pink to the Los40 Music Awards

Last night, Olivia Dean attended the Los40 Music Awards in Barcelona, celebrating a year of global music. And working with stylist Simone Beyene, she selected a striking look for the evening—bringing a pop of pink to the blue carpet.

The dress in question debuted at New York Fashion Week earlier this fall, during Conner Ives’s grand Spring/Summer 2027 return to his hometown. The American designer, who got his start in London after graduating from the city’s Central Saint Martins, crafted the piece-work number from panels of ivory satin, dyed with pink and coral gradients to create a whimsical, airbrushed fish-like pattern.

Delicate spaghetti straps and a square neckline left Dean’s shoulders bare. In the back, the straps dropped into billowing satin, creating a plunging open back silhouette. And from the knees, the shape relaxed into a floor-length skirt that pooled at the singer’s feet.

Hair stylist Sophie Jane Anderson curled Dean’s long locks into a bouncy Old Hollywood blowout with a deep side part, and makeup artist Emily Engleman topped her cheeks with rosy blush.

In addition to performing hit single “Man I Need” at the ceremony, the Art of Loving artist took home the coveted Best International Artist trophy. Accepting the award, she admitted she “wasn’t expecting” it, telling the crowd she was “quite surprised and feeling overwhelmed” with the honor.

“I guess I just want to say thank you. I feel so proud to be an artist and to be an artist that travels the world and be received in other countries,” she continued. “I’m speechless, so I’m just going to go back to my seat now.”

#6659. The Bride Wore Jacquemus—and Went Barefoot—for Her New York City Wedding on a Vintage Yacht

Photographer Anna Watt spent her summers at her family’s home in Montauk growing up. She had just finished her freshman year of college in 2017 when she met Tommy Powell, a second-generation commercial fisherman, at the family-owned bar and restaurant, The Montauket. And what began as a summer fling on Long Island would eventually turn into a nearly decade-long love story. “Over the course of almost 10 years, we always found our way back to each other,” Anna says.

“I introduced myself, but that wasn’t the beginning of ‘us’ just yet,” Tommy recalls. “It took running into her a few more times before I finally convinced her to go on a date with me. Persistence is key!”

“I remember going back to college that fall and telling a friend, ‘I have a feeling I’m going to marry the boy I met this summer,’” Anna says.

As a commercial fisherman, Tommy spends 10 days at sea followed by 10 days on land, a schedule that has shaped the couple’s relationship. Whenever he takes an extended break from fishing, the two make a point of traveling together. In October 2024, they planned a trip to France and Portugal, with surfing and some much-needed time together on the agenda. “When we landed in Paris, I asked what the plan was for the weekend, and Tommy quickly replied with ‘We’re going on a boat tomorrow!’” Anna remembers. “For someone who is typically very go-with-the-flow, I knew what this meant!”

On October 27, 2024, Tommy proposed beneath the Eiffel Tower aboard a small boat on the Seine. (Anna jokes that they like to have all their relationship milestones happen on boats.) “I like to think Anna had no clue it was happening,” Tommy says. “But that wasn’t exactly the reality of the day. That morning, she thought we had no plans, and when I told her we were going on a boat, I think she immediately knew something was up. It was perfect, though—out on the water, with the Eiffel Tower lit up just after sunset.”

Nearly two years later, on September 18, 2026, the couple exchanged vows aboard the Mariner III on the Hudson River in New York City, with 85 of their closest friends and family in attendance. For Anna, who works as a photographer, the wedding was an opportunity to bring her deeply personal vision to life. “I have a very creative type B brain,” Anna says. “I had a very specific vision and designed every detail of the day, down to the silverware, so intentionally.”

Event planner Alex Reiss helped translate Anna’s ideas into reality—including one rather ambitious undertaking. When Anna couldn’t find rental furniture she loved, she enlisted her friend Dewi, an interior designer in Bali, to help her custom-design and import all of the furniture for the boat. “It was such a fun project,” Anna says. “I learned so much, and it ended up being one of my favorite parts of the process!”

The bride’s fashion journey took an equally unexpected turn. “I actually had a completely custom wedding dress made and ready to go,” Anna explains. “But then I saw the Jacquemus spring 2026 runway images and did a complete 180.” After falling for one particular look, she began calling the Jacquemus boutique in SoHo weekly, hoping to track it down. “Finally, this past spring, a sales associate I had been messaging called me and said they had received one,” Anna remembers. “I immediately ran to SoHo with my friends Chris and Hanna to try it on and, somehow, it fit perfectly. Not a single alteration was needed!” It went home with her that day.

A traditional veil didn’t feel quite right with the dress, so Anna commissioned a custom scrunchie to match its trim instead. She kept her jewelry equally understated. “I’ve always been pretty minimal when it comes to jewelry,” she says. “So I wanted to keep everything really simple.” For her something borrowed, she wore a vintage Greek charm bracelet belonging to her mother, while her friend Sophie Thorner, founder of Vice Versa, created custom stud earrings to complement her engagement ring. Another friend, Erin Pollard of Underwater Weaving, made a basket to hold her ceremony flowers, as well as a miniature blue basket for her “something blue.” Her something old was the garter her mother had worn at her own wedding, and for her second look, Anna turned to Laura Tønder of Kettel Atelier, who created a one-of-a-kind dress entirely from vintage crochet and doilies.

Anna made one last-minute adjustment to the bridal look, thanks to the Hudson River itself. “When we hopped onto the boat to hide before guests started arriving, I realized how rocky it was and decided I wanted to ditch my shoes for the ceremony,” Anna remembers. “It just felt right, and I didn’t end up putting my Chloé flats on until we left the boat for the after-party!”

Tommy, meanwhile, chose a navy linen suit by Ralph Lauren Purple Label, paired with white Vans. “I wanted something classic and timeless that still felt right for the setting and the occasion,” Tommy says. “Anna looked absolutely incredible, and seeing her for the first time that day is something I’ll never forget.”

On the wedding day, Anna’s father escorted her down the aisle on the boat’s deck to “Going to California” by Led Zeppelin. “I didn’t have an ounce of nerves,” she says. “I don’t think Tommy did either. We opted to exchange letters the morning of rather than vows as we wanted the ceremony to be light-hearted and fun!”

With the Hudson River and New York City skyline as their backdrop, the couple exchanged vows in a ceremony that was short, sweet, and entirely their own. “I felt so lucky,” Tommy says. “I was marrying my best friend in such a unique place, surrounded by all of the people we love. It was one of those moments where I really tried to take everything in because I knew how special it was.”

“It didn’t feel real!” Anna adds. “When we walked up to the top deck, it was so sunny and bright. Seeing everyone we love all in one place was a crazy feeling I will never forget.”

After the ceremony, guests headed downstairs for cocktail hour, where dirty martinis and French cigarettes set the tone. “The captain of the boat took us right past the Statue of Liberty, which was so insanely cool to see!” Dinner followed upstairs, where custom paper lamps illuminated two long tables. Rather than sit at a sweetheart table, the newlyweds took their places among their guests, right in the middle of the celebration. A family-style meal was served as the boat cruised along the Hudson.

“When I walked up and saw what an amazing job our planner Alex had done, I was blown away,” Anna says. “It truly felt like a once-in-a-lifetime experience having dinner under the George Washington Bridge!”

For Tommy, seeing Anna’s vision come together was one of the most meaningful parts of the weekend. “It was incredibly special, down to every little detail,” he says. “I couldn’t have been more proud of her, of us, and of the incredible job our wedding planner, Alex, did bringing everything together.”

Looking back now, the newlyweds agree they would do it all over again in a heartbeat. “We couldn’t be happier with how the entire night came together,” Tommy says. “It was everything we hoped it would be. It really felt like us.”

“It was perfection!” Anna adds. “I wouldn’t change a thing.”

A quiet moment, just the two of us, before the weekend festivities began.

For my first look, I paired a vintage headscarf from Kettel Atelier with a sculptural vintage fish necklace.

The Hotel Chelsea has always been our go to spot whenever we’re in the city, so it felt only natural to spend our wedding weekend there!

A Jacquemus two-piece set for our welcome drinks!

My wonderful friend Erin of Underwater Weaving made me this little basket bag, which doubled as my purse and my something blue for the weekend.

What happens in St. Tropez apparently follows you home. My bachelorette party ended, but the girls’ chain smoking did not.

Will Metivier and I met on a brand shoot last winter and immediately hit it off. Having him there to do my makeup throughout the wedding weekend made it all the more special!

This Dôen set was a last minute find that ended up being perfect. I also had a hair piece custom made to match the trim of my gown, which I wore in place of a traditional veil!

These Chloe flats from the spring 2025 collection were my very first bridal purchase. They are me in a shoe.

Tommy and I met in 2017! Almost a decade later, this day finally being here felt surreal.

We decided not to have a traditional bridal party, but I invited all of my closest friends to stop by and spend the morning getting ready with me. I loved having everyone come and go!

The Mamma Mia! soundtrack on repeat and a few mimosas to calm the nerves!

My dear friend and stylist Jess Thomas sent me a photo of this Jacquemus dress from the spring 2026 runway, and I knew immediately it was the one.

My something old: my mom’s garter from my parents’ wedding!

Tommy spent the morning with his three older brothers and best friend, Tiaghe.

Our very informal first look quickly dissolved into a fit of laughter, thanks to a less-than-appropriate comment from my mom. Very on brand.

For our portraits, we wandered the cobblestone streets of SoHo.

A quick SoHo smooch! You wouldn’t know it from the photos, but we had quite the audience.

A few quick snaps before we had to sneak away and hide.

We transformed the salon into the perfect lounge space using furniture from our own rental collection, and couldn’t have been happier with how it all came together.

Our embossed cigar matchboxes by MLC Designs.

We couldn’t have asked for a more perfect September day.

Our guests settling into their seats as the ceremony was about to begin.

Tucked away in the master suite of Mariner III, waiting for our guests to arrive and take their seats for the ceremony.

Space is limited on a boat, so we had to get creative! Our friend Dewi helped us custom-design these teak benches and cushions to make the most of the space.

Killing time and sneaking peeks through the porthole window as our guests arrived.

Everyone's faces say it all! My friend Erin of Underwater Weaving also made me the most perfect petite basket for my bridal bouquet.

We told Chris we wanted our ceremony to feel lighthearted, personal, and full of laughter. He understood the assignment! It was so perfectly us.

All smiles! The photos of our guests during the ceremony ended up being some of our favorites. There’s something so special about seeing the joy on the faces of everyone we love most.

The French gifted us a pretty spectacular cocktail hour backdrop.

A rare sighting of Maddy on the other side of the camera.

One of the Mariner III’s deckhands, Eryn Cornelius.

My mom, my aunt, and the New York City skyline.

Tommy’s vintage RRL suspenders were one of my favorite finds of the entire wedding planning process.

Our custom rings, designed by our dear friend Sophie Thorner of Vice Versa Jewelry.

#6658. The Best Gold Nail Polishes, From Soft Champagne to Molten Chrome

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Gold nail polish has a way of making any manicure feel intentional. It can read as quiet luxury on a bare hand, as festive sparkle at a holiday party, or as a modern accent against deep neutrals. But “gold” isn’t one shade. It’s a whole family, and the right pick depends on your skin tone, your style, and the finish you love.

Some golds are warm and buttery, with a champagne glow that flatters nearly everyone. Others lean rich and antique, with the weight of real metal. Then there are glitter-packed formulas that catch the light with every movement, and chrome finishes that look like liquid foil poured over your nails.

To save you the trial and error, we’ve rounded up the best gold nail polish colors, from soft, sheer shimmers to bold metallics that make a statement. Whether you want a subtle hint of shine for everyday wear or a standout shade for the season’s celebrations, there’s a gold here worth adding to your collection.

This antique gold glitter polish shines in two coats on its own or layered over your favorite color.

Golden Cinnamon, a limited-edition shade timed for the holidays, is every bit as luxurious as it sounds: a sparkling gold that catches the light with every gesture.

This gold metallic dries to a rich, opaque finish that gleams like molten metal, no layering or base color required.

For when you’re short on time, this classic quick-dry polish from Sally Hansen delivers fast-drying color and high shine.

Subtle yet radiant, this light pearly gold adds a soft, luminous glow to bare nails or pairs effortlessly with any neutral.

Chanel’s Scintillance delivers gorgeous brilliance in a sheer, golden-champagne shimmer that catches the light with every movement.

Glossy and glittering, this magnetic polish catches the light on its own, but a magnet is what coaxes its metallic particles into their signature shimmer.

Olive & June’s yellow gold version also offers a magnetic effect, which can be styled as velvet, cat-eye, French tip, or circle patterns.

Isla Bonita is a sheer champagne gold with gel-like wear and plenty of shine. Use one coat for a barely-there glimmer or two to three for a full-on golden glow.

Running late for the holiday table? This 3-in-1 folds base coat, color, and top coat into a single swipe, so a polished manicure takes minutes, not an hour. Plus, the shade is the perfect sparkling champagne gold.

For those who want nothing but gold glitter, this topper delivers. Wear it solo for a pared-back shimmer, or layer it over a favorite shade for full-wattage sparkle.

She brightened up her porcelain car coat with a pop of red

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping premiere, the Beauty Inc. Awards, a Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon appearance, and more: Jennifer Lawrence has spent much of the past week all glammed up. On top, she wore a plum-purple T-shirt under a porcelain-beige car coat from the Row, crafted from structured cotton and tailored with a long body lined with silk. For further accessories, the Hunger Games star wore black sunglasses, some Airpods, her go-to gold Sidney Garber necklace, and a small Guidi handbag. The new bag, first spotted on Lawrence’s arm in October, was crafted from black leather with thick rounded straps and shiny silver hardware.

#6656. Through the Meta Lens: A Day on Set With Vogue Shopping’s Market Editor

From documenting fittings to capturing behind-the-scenes styling, my Ray-Ban Meta glasses integrated seamlessly into a day on set. Using them for the first time was remarkably intuitive: they were easy to set up and comfortable to wear, and I was able to put them to use right away. Recording everything as I saw it made the day feel easy (I just had to keep my hair tucked to stop flyaways from brushing the lenses!), letting me upload imagery and share updates with the team in real time.

Set days usually start by me recording fittings and documenting styling moments, which I usually capture pre-shoot—this helps set the tone for the day. I typically capture everything on my phone; this time around I just used my Meta glasses. The day goes by quickly when we’re shooting, and I sometimes forget to capture those fun BTS snippets. After each look has been photographed, I usually take final sitting photos to track the pieces we shot. With my Meta glasses on, I was able to record everything without interrupting the creative flow.

For our most recent dress shoot, we called in a mix of holiday and resort pieces that felt right to wear right now. We went for bold colors (inspired by all the saturated hues seen on the spring runways) and rich textures that were fitting for both everyday wear and end-of-year festivities.

The Meta glasses were an actual game-changer in my process, and I plan to keep using them to capture special everyday moments, at work and at home—particularly those fleeting precious ones of my young daughter.

Inspired by several of Celine’s tonal spring looks, I wanted to bring this liveliness into the holidays with a similar bold color palette.

To play up the drama on this Dries Van Noten gown, I wanted to go all out with accessories. Enter: a shearling cape, opera-length leather gloves, and a pair of statement earrings. Together, they lean into its main character energy.

Knit dresses are a given in the winter. Instead of going with a simple rib, I wanted a strong textural moment. This bouclé style was a natural choice. To zhuzh it up, I pinned this Lié Studio brooch on it, adding knee-high boots and a patterned clutch as finishing touches.

The cummerbund isn’t going anywhere any time soon! Here, it wraps around a red Róhe maxi dress, which I paired with Khaite’s mini zebra bag and a pair of black kitten heels for a graphic pop.

The idea behind this ensemble was all about contrast—achieved here by pairing a deep berry Fforme dress in hammered satin with a yellow velvet Ossou jacket. I kept accessories to a minimum with a simple duo of pendant necklaces.

#6655. Inside Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando’s Wedding Ceremony and the Vows They Exchanged

Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando got married on Saturday, and the singer shared the first look at their wedding photos—and her backless Saint Laurent dress—yesterday. Sources also revealed more about the nuptials and vow exchange with Entertainment Tonight and People.

Entertainment Tonight reported that Cyrus expressed her hope to start a family with Morando in her vows. “Before I met you I was lost, and in finding you I found myself,” she said. “Creating with you is my all-time favorite thing, which is why I can’t wait to make a baby! I hope our baby has your hair, but mostly I hope that it has your sweet spirit.”

Morando, meanwhile, told her, “I’m going to be the husband who makes you feel safe and supported. I want to show up for you and our family everyday...I’m a better version of myself because of you.”

A source told People that Cyrus was emotional during the exchange. “It was such a beautiful ceremony,” the insider said. “Miley was excited and a little nervous beforehand. During the vows, she kept smiling through her tears. She was trying to hold it together, but she was just so happy to be marrying Maxx.”

Guests included the Bass Persuades singer’s blended family. Her mother, Tish Cyrus-Purcell, came with her husband Dominic Purcell, while her father, Billy Ray Cyrus, attended with his girlfriend, Elizabeth Hurley.

“The most special part [of the day] was seeing Miley’s family all come together to celebrate her,” a source told People. “They wanted her to feel loved and for her to have a magical wedding day. Knowing how much it took to get to that point, seeing them all together was really moving.”

Cyrus hasn’t said much about her ceremony yet. She captioned the Instagram post with her wedding photos simply: “M + M 🤍 11.21.26”⁠

#6654. Hailey Bieber’s 30 Best Looks in Honor of Her 30th Birthday

From polka dots and fur to red-carpet statements

Happy birthday, Hailey Bieber! The star has officially turned 30, and to mark another turn around the sun, she kicked off a week of celebrations with a new navy-blue Rhode drop, a festive campaign, and an intimate video series that followed a week in her life. Throughout the vlogs, we saw the founder in fittings and makeup chairs, spending time with son Jack Blues, and reflecting on the past decade. “Becoming a mom definitely changed me the most in my twenties,” she told the camera. “I always knew I wanted to be a mom, I always knew I wanted kids, and it just totally transforms you as a person for the better.”

Of course, the birth-week celebrations have also come with a wardrobe to match. From shearling coats to archival statements, she ushered in the new season with everything from an ivory satin Oriori coat trimmed in gray-white fur to a black silk Armani Privé Fall 2005 set to a Yohji Yamamoto Spring 1998 jacket previously seen on Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy. And we did not expect anything less from the star.

Throughout the years, Bieber has become as known for her style as for her Rhode lipgloss phone cases, playing with understated “quiet luxury,” classic Los Angeles athleisure, and tons of Saint Laurent leather. As she grew from a teenage model into a business owner and, later, young mother, her taste has evolved over time—but through it all, she has given us some major fashion inspiration.

So, in honor of her 30th birthday, we rounded up our 30 favorite looks from the star. And between her plethora of Met Gala ensembles, polka-dot prints, and mismatched moments with husband Justin, there was a lot to pick from.

For the New York Times Dealbook Summit, Bieber takes a page from Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy and wears a Yohji Yamamoto Spring 1998 jacket previously worn by the late It girl.

Stepping out in New York City, Bieber pairs her Phoebe Philo cropped fur coat with blue jeans and vintage Manolos.

The star wears the coat of the season: Conner Ives’s reconstituted fur robe in white silk mikado.

Bieber wears an iridescent jacket from Matthieu Blazy’s Chanel Fall 2026 collection. With a medley of silver, red, and turquoise mesh, the piece puts an aluminum chainmail twist on the house’s signature tweed.

For the Academy Museum Gala, Bieber wears a custom bubblegum-pink Chanel dress.

At the 2026 Vanity Fair Oscar after-party, she hits the carpet wearing a shimmering leopard-print gown, made custom by Armani Privé. She accessorizes with Lorraine Schwartz jewelry and Manolo Blahnik heels.

While in Tokyo, Bieber wears a textured Issey Miyake egg-carton skirt suit from the Fall/Winter 2000 collection.

Doing press in Australia, Bieber wears a green Valentino Spring 2026 minidress, with structured shoulders, ruching, and a sweet bow at the hem.

Bieber attends the GQ Men Of The Year party in a naked dress and sparkly Gucci thong, bringing back the ’90s trend.

At the 2025 Academy Museum Gala, Bieber steps out in a striking, sculptural gown from Schiaparelli, constructed from brown moiré vintage ribbons for the house’s Spring/Summer 2025 Haute Couture runway.

Supporting Kylie Jenner at the Kylie Cosmetics anniversary event, Bieber looks to Wiederhoeft for a belted satin midi dress, designed with a chunky belt and thigh-high slit.

While out for an evening in New York, Bieber turns heads in an electric green minidress from Dolce & Gabbana’s 2003 collection.

Stepping out in New York, Bieber embraces two of the year's biggest trends—polka dots and capris—all in one go.

Bieber wears a Marine Serre dress made out of metallic-silver watch straps for a weekend in Miami during the Grand Prix.

Bieber spends an NYC evening at Cafe Zaffri, wearing a silky ice-blue minidress—a vintage Gucci piece from the fashion house’s Spring/Summer 1998 collection, designed by Tom Ford.

Leaving Funk in Los Angeles with Justin, Hailey is seen in an oversized gray suit with strong shoulders and baggy trousers, paired with a burgundy tie and matching clutch.

Stepping out with Justin, who matches his wife's Adidas with a pop of red, Hailey layers on the leopard print patterns—pairing a matching trench and shoulder bag from Saint Laurent.

Bieber highlights her bump with a silky white asymmetrical minidress and matching square-toe heels.

For her pregnancy announcement, Bieber poses in a bridal long-sleeve Saint Laurent maxi dress and matching lacy veil, with chunky sunglasses for a full old Hollywood glam look.

Captured in what have since become iconic photos, Hailey and Justin take couples dressing to new contrasting heights, with her in a little red dress and him in a gray hoodie and Crocs.

Glove shoes are certainly having a moment. Made from soft, pliable leather that molds to the foot, they often feature a higher vamp than traditional shoes and come in everything from flats to heels and boots. The style showed up across both the fall and spring runways, with high fashion designers giving it plenty of attention. Naturally, that makes us pay attention to it, too. Ahead, dive into the trend and shop it for yourself.

If you really want to be the most fashion-forward person in your office (without looking like a clown), wear a pair of glove heels to your next board meeting. It’s a subtle swap that fashion insiders will immediately recognize. My personal favorites are from Bottega Veneta and 3.1 Phillip Lim.

Proenza Schouler Glove 70MM Leather Pumps

Now, when it comes to glove boots, your options are a bit more limited. That said, if any of these pairs speak to you, I recommend jumping on the chance to make them yours. Whether you go for a flat or heeled rendition, these are a sleek alternative to your average winter boot.

#6652. Everything We Know About Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando’s Wedding

Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando just said “I do.” On Saturday, November 21, the former Disney Channel star and her drummer fiancé tied the knot in Palm Springs, surrounded by family and friends.

The newlyweds first met on a blind date back in 2021, and have been linked for the five years since. In the time between, they have kept their relationship fairly private and out of the spotlight, simply popping up for the rare red-carpet appearance or supporting one another at a performance. Behind the scenes, the two have proven avid collaborators, working together on Cyrus’s Something Beautiful and Bass Persuades records.

In December of 2025, Cyrus announced her engagement in the subtle (yet not-so-subtle) manner of debuting a chunky gold engagement ring at the Hollywood premiere of Avatar: Fire and Ash—letting the shimmering diamond do all the talking.

Despite keeping things out of the public eye, Cyrus offered a rare glimpse into her life with Morando during her Harper’s Bazaar December 2024/January 2025 cover story interview. “He’s very similar to me,” she said of her beau, a drummer for the rock band Liily. “We just don’t take life too seriously.”

Ahead, we take a look at everything we know about Cyrus and Morando’s wedding.

Cyrus and Morando’s wedding ceremony took place in Palm Springs, California. More specifically, it was held at Frank Sinatra’s former home, which was transformed with hundreds of white roses for the occasion. Photos obtained exclusively by DeuxMoi showed the couple exchanging vows by the pool, in front of an intimate crowd of guests.

The couple’s official photos showed the “Can’t Be Tamed” star wearing a white long-sleeve Saint Laurent gown with an open back and long train. She paired the look with an updo, drop earrings, and pointed-toe heels, and had her Jacquie Aiche-designed engagement ring on full display. Standing with her at the altar, Morando wore a classic suit—matching the guests, who were all dressed in black.

At the ceremony—which was officiated by Flaming Lips frontman Wayne Coyne—Cyrus and Morando were surrounded by friends and family. Among the guests were Cyrus’s parents, Tish and Billy Ray, with their respective partners, Dominic Purcell and Elizabeth Hurley.

#6651. Amelia Dimoldenberg Brought Her Chicken Shop Date Break-Up Tour to Metrograph

“All good dates must come to an end.” This is how Amelia Dimoldenberg announced to the world, back in September, that she was signing off from her beloved YouTube series Chicken Shop Date. To officially say goodbye, she gathered a crowd that boasted past dates, friends, New York City crushes, and media personalities at Metrograph.

What started as a youth club project has, over the last 12 years, garnered Dimoldenberg cult status and a devout following. The Londoner’s intentionally awkward and endearing deadpan interviews with stars like Cher, Paul McCartney, Billie Eilish, Jennifer Lawrence, and Daniel Kaluuya weren’t just entertaining, they also successfully re-contextualized the typical celebrity interview setup—with a side of nuggets, chips, and neon lighting in humble fast-food spots for a dose of levity. Whether she was asking Jack Harlow if he could read, matching Alex Consani’s frenetic energy, creating ear-worms with Louis Theroux (who could forget “My money don’t jiggle, jiggle, it folds”), or fueling romantic fan-fic with her off-the-Richter chemistry with Andrew Garfield, Dimoldenberg consistently created memorable viral moments.

The finale is set to premiere in theaters across the U.K. and U.S. on November 24, before dropping on YouTube on November 27. Final-season guests have included Jorja Smith, Noel Gallagher, Nemzzz, Role Model, and Jack O’Connell (a.k.a. Cook from Skins: every millennial’s formative bad-boy pin-up). But on this night, in Metrograph’s theater one, Dimoldenberg let a few people in on the secret before the rest of the world, revealing the last episode and the much-anticipated closing guest.

“It’s bittersweet, but I feel so ready to do the next thing,” Dimoldenberg told Vogue ahead of the screening. Sitting in the empty theater in a sparkling lace dress by Mandalay, she explained that the decision to end the show was 18 months in the making. “It’s been a process to get there. And that’s why I feel like this is more of a celebration. It would be a weird vibe if I was just sad,” she joked.

For the Thursday night outing, attendees including Sean Evans, Richie Shazam, Jon Caramanica, Joe Coscarelli, and Gabby Bryan laughed and made fast friends over dirty martinis, tart margaritas, and Chicken Shop Date-branded bags of popcorn. As Dimoldenberg made the rounds, she lit up and squealed when Harlow sauntered into the room wearing baggy pants and an oatmeal-hued knit pullover. The two embraced with a warm hug, as Mel Ottenberg—who swapped his denim uniform for a slick suit—chatted with comedian Stavros Halkias. Eventually, the giddy crowd began slinking toward their seats for the main event.

“You’ve become something of a celebrity, Amelia,” The New Yorker’s Naomi Fry remarked, in a short panel before the show. “I know, it’s so embarrassing,” Dimoldenberg replied dryly.

The series was aired in its entirety, and as the final episode concluded, there was some unmistakable sniffling, and even some tears. The closing credits gave way to a swell of applause, as cheers for the star filled the room. “I think that final episode had to be about me,” Dimoldenberg confessed earlier. In hindsight, it all made sense. With a rom-com in development, which she’s also featuring in, Dimoldenberg has plans beyond the internet now, hoping to one day direct, too. It was a farewell that not only centered her trajectory as the show’s host but also closed the chapter on this part of her career.

The theater had emptied, and upstairs a party had begun. Guests stretched across leather booths, sipped on cocktails, and excitedly exchanged their reviews of the final episode. The only thing seemingly missing was chicken. Not for long, though, as chicken parm sliders soon arrived. All good dates must come to an end, but this one ended the right way.

#6650. Louis Vuitton Takes Its Place at the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix Finish Line

A handcrafted trunk awaited the winner, Max Verstappen.

When Max Verstappen crossed the finish line at the Las Vegas Formula 1 Grand Prix on Saturday night, after a gripping race that saw the championship driver battle to maintain the tightest of leads against rivals George Russell and Kimi Antonelli, his trophy came in very special packaging: a bespoke Louis Vuitton trunk. For the past two seasons, Trophy Trunks have been presented to the winner of the annual Las Vegas event, which sees drivers race on a thrilling course that winds along the famous Strip. They have also been presented to the winners of the World Cup, America’s Cup, and the NBA Finals. Louis Vuitton had a strong presence across the whole race weekend, hosting a suite where guests including Teyana Taylor watched the events from above the track and were able to get an early look at the trunk.

The Las Vegas trunk was, like all Louis Vuitton custom pieces, made at Asnières-sur-Seine, a commune in northern France. It was handcrafted by 25 artisans, made to the specific dimensions of the trophy. The Trophy Trunks are a remarkable mingling of the old and the new. They use the traditional craftsmanship techniques that have defined the house for over 170 years. All construction of the trunks’ wood, leather, and locks was done with the same techniques LV has used since the beginning, meaning that in many ways the Trophy Trunks differ little from its trunks from a century ago. The modern energy of motor racing comes through via subtle touches like the two stripes across the trunk that make a large V, a nod to both Vuitton and victory—they’re black-and-white checkered as a nod to the Formula 1 finish line. A small badge that calls back to the early days of trunk travel and bears the winning driver’s initials was added this year.

Louis Vuitton’s relationship with Formula 1 began with the Grand Prix de Monaco, which the brand began creating Trophy Trunks for in 2021. In 2025, it became an official partner of the league, and this year, LV created trunks for all 24 of the season’s races. In early December, the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix will mark the final 2026 race.

#6649. Miley Cyrus Turns to Saint Laurent’s Anthony Vaccarello for a Backless Wedding Dress

The star married Maxx Morando in Palm Springs

Miley Cyrus is a bride—a Saint Laurent bride, that is. Yesterday, the “Wrecking Ball” singer married longtime partner Maxx Morando at an intimate, flower-covered Palm Springs ceremony.

In new photos shared directly by Cyrus, the woman of the hour was seen wearing a timeless white gown, designed by Anthony Vaccarello for Saint Laurent. The whole dress was crafted from silk, and featured long sleeves, an open plunging back, and a train that pooled at her feet. Styled by Bradley Kenneth, it was paired with a matching set of silk slingback heels.

The decision to work with Saint Laurent was not unexpected, given Cyrus’s long-standing partnership with the house. Most recently, the star was seen in Vaccarello’s designs at the 2026 Golden Globes and during her Hollywood Bowl shows in October. The wedding dress, however, was likely one of the creative director’s final big moments with the label, as his departure was announced last month.

For glam, Cyrus went bold, styling her hair in an updo and giving her eyes a smokey shadow. Her stack of diamonds was the perfect blend of classic glamour and rockstar edge (the best of both worlds, if you will), with drop Chopard earrings, studs, and a crawler that curved upward along the ear.

Morando, too, wore Saint Laurent. Sitting next to his wife on a leather chair, he was seen in a black single-breasted tuxedo with a silk-satin tie. He added in his own rockstar edge with a pair of grained-leather sneakers and sunglasses.

A first look at the ceremony, obtained exclusively by DeuxMoi, showed the couple—who first started dating back in 2021, after being set up on a blind date—standing amongst white roses. The nuptials took place at Frank Sinatra’s former home, with Flaming Lips frontman Wayne Coyne reportedly serving as officiant. All of the guests appeared to be wearing black, including Cyrus’s parents, Tish and Billy Ray, and their respective partners, Dominic Purcell and Elizabeth Hurley.

#6648. All About Gabbriette Bechtel, Matty Healy’s Wife

Matty Healy, lead singer of The 1975, has been in a relationship with model and influencer Gabbriette Bechtel since late 2023. In an interview with Highsnobiety published in March 2024, Bechtel candidly shared her feelings regarding the internet’s constant speculation about them.

“I don’t give a shit. I think it’s hilarious. Go for it. Have fun. People have a lot to say,” she laughed. “You don’t know me at all.”

Arguably, Healy’s most well-known relationship came just before he began seeing Bechtel. From May to June 2023, the singer briefly and memorably dated Taylor Swift. The musicians first met in 2014, and while relationship rumors swirled over the years, the two were never official. Swift’s album, The Tortured Poets Department, has even been rumored to be about Healy.

But he and Bechtel have gotten far more serious over their three years of dating and now—marriage! So, who is Healy’s wife? Ahead, everything to know about Bechtel and her relationship with Healy.

Healy and Bechtel’s relationship timeline begins in September 2023. In some photos obtained by People, the pair is seen kissing, hugging, and holding hands while walking together in New York City.

They continued to have PDA sightings, like in November, when they were spotted with their arms wrapped around each other in New York.

Things seem to be getting serious between them by February 2024, when Bechtel was seen spending time with Healy’s family. Photos came out of Healy and Bechtel heading to the theater to watch his mother Denise Welch’s play The Gap. Also in attendance was Healy’s brother, as well as his father, Tim Healy, and his wife.

Previously, in October 2023, Welch showed Bechtel some support on her Instagram. When the model posted a photo wearing nothing but a G-string thong and leather apron from her collaboration with R & M Leathers, Healy’s mom commented, “That’s exactly how I hope to look in mine when it arrives!! 👍👍👍❤️❤️❤️.”

On June 11, the couple announced they were engaged after attending Charli XCX’s Brat Tour show in Brooklyn. Bechtel shared photos of herself wearing the ring, which she was first spotted wearing in May, according to People. The ring has a black diamond in the center that is surrounded by white diamonds.

“MARRYING THE 1975 IS VERY BRAT,” she wrote in the caption.

Denise Welch, Healy’s mom, confirmed the engagement on Loose Women the following day.

“I obviously have known for a few weeks that Matty got engaged,” she said. “They went over to see their friends Charli and George in New York [last night] and I woke up this morning to the fact they’ve put it on Instagram. Instagram official...he’s got engaged to Gabriella Bechtel—Gabbriette she’s known as. Black diamond; he had it made for her...I couldn’t be more thrilled. We couldn’t be happier—she is everything I would want in a daughter-in-law. I’m thrilled.”

The couple was photographed at the O2 Silver Clef Awards on Friday, July 5, sharing a quiet conversation outside Grosvenor House Hotel in London. Bechtel leaned into Healy and kissed him on his cheek. The 1975 frontman was wearing a navy blazer with jeans, and the model wore a black dress with a turtleneck and a pair of black heels. During the ceremony, The 1975 won the Best Group award.

Signaling that they were still going strong in the new year, Bechtel and Healy were spotted on a date in Los Angeles on Jan. 9, 2026. They were photographed walking arm-in-arm to Wilde’s for dinner, a restaurant in Los Feliz. They were both dressed casually in jeans, with Healy wearing a dark cardigan over a white T-shirt and Bechtel in a blazer with rows of gold buttons.

On July 18, Healy and Bechtel were married in Los Angeles at Castillo del Lago, which was formerly owned by Madonna. They appeared kissing at the altar in photos. Bechtel wore a long-sleeve gown with a drop waist and a full floor-length skirt. She had her hair half up with a veil pinned in back. Healy wore a classic black tux and bow tie.

“Matty Healy and Gabbriette Bechtel were married yesterday at a private ceremony in Los Angeles, attended by their family and close friends,” reps for the couple told People.

In an August 2026 interview with Harper’s Bazaar, Bechtel opened up about her impressions of married life with Healy.

“I don’t feel like it’s gonna be very different,” she said. “I feel like I’ve already met my best friend.…The wedding is for our moms and dads. I wanted to do, like, a 50-person thing in a field, so.”

In November 2026, Bechtel and Healy were photographed together in Los Angeles while attending Jessie Jo Stark’s Muse album release celebration. The couple’s outing sparked pregnancy rumors on social media.

Days later, on November 22, People reported that Bechtel and Healy were expecting their first baby together. The news came after the couple was snapped shopping at Bristol Farms in West Hollywood, with Bechtel’s pregnant figure visible in a fitted black dress.

In a May 2023 interview with Vogue, Bechtel shared that she was born and raised in Orange County, and originally moved to Los Angeles to pursue her dream of becoming a professional ballerina.

“I was convinced I was going to be a professional ballerina, and I still am,” she said.

However, her career plans shifted after she was cast by MTV to dance in music videos for Blood Orange (Dev Hynes).

“I put a few dance videos on my Instagram, and somebody reached out to me and said that Dev was having an open call,” she told Highsnobiety. “We had a few fun days of rehearsal and started to film the music video, and then I got a call that I was cut. I didn’t make it into the music video, but I did all of the rehearsals, and I think my feet are in it at some point.”

“I was an unpaid, hard-working model for a very long time,” Bechtel revealed.

Now, Bechtel has modeled for brands like Heaven by Marc Jacobs, Diesel, Miu Miu, and Betsey Johnson. On April 15, 2024, she graced the cover of HommeGirls.

Bechtel is multitalented. In 2019, she was handpicked by Charli XCX to be the lead singer of a band called Nasty Cherry for a Netflix documentary series, I’m with the Band: Nasty Cherry.

“I met [Charli XCX] on the set of a music video, and we ended up partying together for a few years,” she recalls. “I didn’t see her for a while, and then she reached out and was like, ‘I’m doing this project and I’ve been trying to cast the singer…’” Bechtel told Highsnobiety.

Unfortunately, Nasty Cherry is no longer active, with the group choosing to disband during the COVID-19 pandemic.

“We couldn’t do anything together, we couldn’t tour our second EP, and we weren’t able to make music together because we were all in different places in the world. So we just decided that it wasn’t going to work out anymore,” she revealed. “I miss it all the time. It ended too abruptly.”

Bechtel also has a social media presence. Aside from her 1.6 million followers on Instagram, she has amassed 840,400 on TikTok, where she mostly posts cooking videos. In May 2023, she posted a video recreating Erewhon’s grain-free vegan blackout cake, which garnered 3 million views.

Per Highsnobiety, Bechtel shared that she got her love of cooking from her Mexican mother and Swiss-German father, both of whom would cook food from their respective cultures.

“We ate dinner together as a family every single night, so there was always a fresh meal. We never had takeout,” she recalled. “We had a lot of Bon Appétit magazines lying around, so [my mother] would always try new recipes. I would come home and she’d have it open and be like, ‘I’m making this tonight,’ and she’d nail it. I would help her prep, so I grew up with my mom testing out stuff.”

She also shared with Vogue that she is working on a cookbook and eventually would love to open up her own café.

“Not many people know this, but I’m really into interior design. So I’d love to open a space so people can have the full experience,” Bechtel said.

Bechtel was born on July 28, 1997, making her a Leo. Healy, 37, was born on April 8, making him an Aries. According to the AstroTwins, per ELLE.com, “A pair of dynamic fire signs, Aries and Leo make a head-turning duo that whips up passion, adventure, and a heavy dose of drama everywhere you go. A flashy, outspoken pair, you’ll inspire envy. Get ready to reinvent the rules of relationships since your connection is certain to play by its own bold agenda.”

#6647. The Under-The-Radar Brands the Best Dressed List Loved in 2026

Vogue’s 2026 best dressed list certainly knows its way around a luxury label ambassadorship: Chanel swans, Saint Laurent savants, Dior devotees, Miu Miu girls and Prada protégés. But along the way, you’ll find that some of this year’s most thrilling moments for ‘stepping out’ and ‘stunning’ (as per the celebrity style news cycle) came courtesy of designers whose names aren’t quite so familiar. For this particularly discerning crowd, an emerging designer and an IYKYK label carries just a bit more sartorial currency.

The distinction between under-the-radar and fashion-crowd famous is becoming increasingly blurred. Designers like Conner Ives and Rachel Scott’s Diotima have developed considerable celebrity followings and their fair share of viral moments, while labels like Kallmeyer are hardly insider secrets anymore. The next generation, however, is hot on their heels.

Greta Lee, Hunter Schafer, and Whitney Peak have embraced the retro-futurist designs of Zane Li’s Lii, the award-winning label crafted from his unassuming and tiny Chinatown studio. Tessa Thompson, Ayo Edebiri, and Paloma Elsesser, meanwhile, found plenty to love in Giovanna Flores’s free-form silhouettes, pattern agnosticism, and deadstock materials. Elsewhere, Elle Fanning indulged in the character play of August Barron, Jenna Ortega put a young designer’s extraordinary corsetry craftsmanship on the red carpet, and John Malkovich looked to upcycled lace. Rosalía has made something of a habit of championing emerging talent, with the likes of Yasmina Atta and Laura Andraschko finding a place in her expansive, prima ballerina meets bad-girl Mary Magdalene wardrobe.

More than a passing fascination with the next big thing, this year’s best dressed list has fostered relationships with designers in ways that speak to their genuine curiosity and enthusiasm about clothes, the people making them, and the exciting places fashion is heading. Below, the under-the-radar brands this year’s best dressed loved.

Brooklyn-based Giovanna Flores is a fast favorite among Hollywood’s most adventurous dressers for her scavenger-chic designs. Her work is often made using deadstock and recycled textiles, and utilizes unexpected fabric combinations, patchworking, and inventive draping. Paloma Elsesser dropped her polka dot bodice and zebra-hemmed G.F. fit amid one fab Instagram dump, and Tessa Thompson mixed her prints with a sumptuous Bordeaux sash. Ayo Edebiri opted for a mismatched strawberry seed and gingham number, while Greta Lee wore some canary yellow velvet. (Both Edebiri and Lee are styled by Danielle Goldberg and hold Chanel and Dior ambassador titles respectively—Flores’s spliced-and-diced one-of-ones are a must-have.)

Zane Li’s Lii is a fashion-crowd secret hiding in plain sight; this year, he netted the LVMH Karl Lagerfeld Prize for Innovation and was a CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund winner. Known for its architectural minimalism and precise construction in enchanting color combos, the New York label has struck a major chord. Greta Lee, again, was an early champion, most recently wearing an architectural two-toned blue dress with a sexy thigh-high slit. Whitney Peak wore a twisted tank and skirt look fresh from the spring 2027 runway—a collection that unspooled the emotional threads between girlhood and womanhood, reflected in dramatically skewed tops and miniskirts in scuba materials and wide-eyed shades of teal and tomato. Hunter Schafer has incorporated the retro-futurist designs into her ongoing Blade Runner 2099 press tour. Consider Lii a modern fixture in the wardrobes of Hollywood’s experimental minimalists.

Rosalía has spent the last year either en pointe or expounding the possibilities of a popstar’s wardrobe, oscillating between the ecclesiastical and the balletic. London-based, Nigerian-born designer Yasmina Atta, a Central Saint Martins graduate whose surrealist designs draw on African cinema, folklore, and subculture, was central to one of Rosalía’s most viral fashion moments. This was when she stepped out in New York in a custom Atta creation: a plunging, sheer bronze latex bodice, visible black lace lingerie, a dramatically dropped waist, and a frothy cream tutu, all cinched with studded belts—a look partly inspired by Edgar Degas’s Little Dancer Aged Fourteen. (Rosalía had also worn a slate-gray wool minidress by the designer earlier in the year.) For a musician whose Lux era has been defined by religious iconography and the discipline of dance, Atta’s fantastical yet fervent approach to fashion is a perfect fit.

Laura Andraschko’s hedonistic, subculture-informed designs also found a fan in Rosalía. The Berlin- and Vienna-raised Central Saint Martins graduate draws on various influences: indie sleaze and nightlife, aristocrats, Sloane Rangers, and Alpine bunny glam. Rosalía has worn the designer on several occasions: at the 2026 US Open, she chose an Andraschko T-shirt, while a previous Paris outing saw her in a khaki minidress from the fall 2025 Après Ski collection, with a dramatic furry hem and velvet-trimmed, off-the-shoulder neckline. More recently, of course, she had to pull on a tutu-like skirt. It’s feminine and anarchic and exactly right for Rosalía.

Jenna Ortega and her stylist Enrique Melendez spent last year crafting a deviant glam-goth wardrobe for the Wednesday star. This year, we’ve witnessed a subtle evolution into freer experiments with color and textiles. For a New York screening of Klara and the Sun, Ortega wore a sculptural creation by young designer Elias Matso, made from steel corset boning and 6,500 beads, all inspired by the colors of painter Marc Ranger. The Polimoda graduate’s approach to corsetry is theatrical and technically audacious, with references ranging from Bob Mackie to Charles James. The custom dress reportedly took more than 300 hours to make, and marked a major red carpet moment for a designer early in his career.

“This dress was a massive test of my free will and just how much I was willing to put towards something that did not have a guaranteed return,” Matso said. “It was scary, I felt crazy at times, I lost a lot of money, and now this object exists. After many blisters, rebuilds, failed trials, international shipping nightmares, and working on it in six different cities with so many helping hands it just exists, and that is wild.” A hand-crafting corsetier to know.

Elle Fanning is all about the Effie-coded whimsy right now, and Paris-based August Barron has proven a kindred spirit in this quest. Formerly known as All-In, the label is the brainchild of Benjamin Barron and Bror August Vestbø, whose designs play with heady ideas of domesticity, nostalgia, and the conventions of femininity. Fanning made a memorable appearance in a pale yellow striped polo shirt and a voluminous, bow-adorned tulle skirt from their fall 2026 Bedtime Story collection. The design duo has a talent for taking familiar clothes and articulating something thrilling throught them. Whether referencing American pageant girls, cabaret queens, housewives, gay icons Judy or a Marilyn, August Barron provides the much-needed glitch in the glamour for those brave enough to dial in.

London-based GOYAGOMA was the talk of London Fashion Week when the label made its debut earlier this year at designer incubator Fashion East (the same one that birthed Simone Rocha, Martine Rose, and Grace Wales Bonner.) Of course, Paloma Elsesser picked up his designs fast, and previous best dressed honoree A$AP Rocky is a fan. Founded by Bahamian designer Traiceline Pratt, a Central Saint Martins graduate who previously worked with Phoebe Philo and A-Cold-Wall, the label draws on memories of growing up in the Bahamas to reimagine everyday clothing through luxe fabrications, exaggerated proportions, and determined tailoring. Elsesser’s endorsement adds to an already growing list of admirers of the designer’s assuredly off-beat approach to the capsule wardrobe—expect to see it hit Dover Street Market soon, too.

Julie Kegels takes her bow during spring 2027.

Antwerp-born Julie Kegels has established herself as one of the most interrogative young voices in European fashion, and both Paloma Elsesser and Rosalia have taken notice. A graduate of Antwerp’s Royal Academy of Fine Arts who went on to work at Alaïa, Kegels launched her namesake label in 2024, exploring the tension between conventional feminine dressing and something more surreal. Her collections manipulate familiar silhouettes through draping and distortion, taking as much inspiration from working girls as she does from furniture. Winning the 2026 LVMH Prize has only accelerated her ascent—her signature thong socks are an even speedier way into the brand, or you could hold out for her plans to invest her LVMH prize money into the development of more shoes and bags.

Miyako Bellizzi styled and walked the spring 2027 show

Founded by Stella Ishii in 2013, with Lizzie Owens now leading design, New York label 6397 has built a quietly influential universe of lived-in separates and pieces that slyly riff on what “staples” can mean. Among its fans are Paloma Elsesser, Greta Lee, and Sarah Pidgeon. The brand’s debut runway show was styled by costume designer and best dressed lister Miyako Bellizzi, who also walked in the presentation. The downtown creative community has long embraced 6397, and this is the New York woman energy you just want to bottle.

Whitney Peak wears spring 2026, styled by Karla Welch.

London-based Torishéju takes an experimental and emotive approach to pattern-cutting and construction: trained as a menswear designer, Torishéju Dumi has built a sartorial world that plays with trompe l’oeil and other-century costuming made modern, combining subversive design twists and classic craft techniques. Whitney Peak, on The Hunger Games press tour, opted for a deconstructed scarlet red leather skirt brought together by sensual draping and thigh-high cutouts, paired with a sculpted black halter top. This is the one for those who like their fashion with a little friction.

Never underestimate the power of a great pair of trousers. And as Ayo Edebiri knows, the best off-duty outfits often hinge on an immaculate basic. Her choice? Still Kelly’s tailored black trousers worn with a vintage Björk T-shirt sourced by stylist Danielle Goldberg. The brand describes itself as a sartorial “slow burn.” “Building a world, making good products, it takes time,” founder Marc Kalman previously told Vogue. “I’m cool with that.”

Louisa Jacobson has never been one for fashion’s binaries. With stylist Edward Bowleg III, she delights in the push-and-pull of buttoned-up tailoring and daring exposure, masculine codes and feminine flourishes. Catalogue NYC is exactly the sort of emerging designer label that articulates that. Founded by former Peter Do designers Pablo Correa and An Nguyen alongside Vincent Ho, the New York brand approaches familiar wardrobe pieces with an experimental eye, proposing new ways of wearing tailoring and dresses. On Jacobson, those ideas find an exquisite home.

A saucy sliver of toe and a beckoning, warped heel have become immediately identifiable Jude signatures. The Paris-based footwear label was founded in 2024 by Jurgita Dileviciute and Denitsa Bumbarova, and the duo’s subtly subversive designs take familiar shoe silhouettes and give them a deliciously peculiar twist—most notably with their barely-there peep toes. Zoë Kravitz is a fan of the Date pump, while Sarah Pidgeon favors the Date mule. Tracee Ellis Ross has amassed a well-curated collection of Jude footwear, from the sinuous Fame pump to the Haze sandal. It’s little wonder the label has found favor with fashion’s freakiest feet: Jude knows that even the smallest detail can demand a double take at the dogs.

#6646. Princess Kate Opens Up About Her Cancer Journey in a New Documentary

”There’s a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you,” she reflected on camera

Since announcing her cancer diagnosis in March of 2024, Princess Kate has been open with the public about her treatment, remission, and what the experience has taught her about life. But now, she is taking things even deeper with Heal, a documentary centered around the royal’s recovery journey.

With never-before-seen footage and personal testimonies, the film followed Kate as she undertook the National Three Peaks Challenge last June, in support of the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity. The trailer for the project, which will premiere in the United Kingdom on November 29 before reaching the United States the day after, showed the Princess of Wales celebrating the accomplishment, meeting with others impacted by cancer, and contemplating the ways in which she has been changed since her diagnosis.

“Cancer does change you,” Kate said on camera. “It changes your body, it changes you physically. But there’s a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you.”

In one scene, the future queen was seen at the end of her climb, where she was joined by her family. The first to embrace her was Princess Charlotte who ran up to her mother for a hug. Prince Louis then joined in, and Prince William and Prince George followed suit.

“Healing is a journey, how to reconnect with the things you once knew and how to find a sense of hope and joy alongside uncertainty,” the princess continued. “Things can renew and grow, and often it is through pain we realize there’s a greater beauty that lies beyond that.”
